2297834.title: Government Strengthens Access to National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for SC Students
2297834.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Access to National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for SC Students
580 Students Awarded Scholarships and Enrolled Abroad Under the Scheme from 2019-20 to 2025-26
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has stated that a total of 580 students have been awarded scholarships and enrolled abroad under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme for Scheduled Castes during the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26 (till August 6, 2026).

The written reply was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in response to Shri Daggumalla Prasada Rao in the Lok Sabha.

According to the information furnished by the Ministry, 41 students received scholarships in 2019-20, followed by 71 in 2020-21, 98 in 2021-22, 98 in 2022-23, 114 in 2023-24, 80 in 2024-25 and 78 in 2025-26.

To raise awareness about the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme among students, relevant details including scheme guidelines and instructions are posted on the Departmental website.

The Minister further submitted that advertisements are also published in newspapers and letters are sent to the Social Welfare Departments of State Governments and Union Territories with a request for widespread publicity of the Scheme.

Applications under the NOS Scheme are invited through the online portal. The Scheme has recently been onboarded to the newly launched unified SAMAVESH (Single Access Mechanism for All Verticals of Empowerment & Social Harmony) Portal, to streamline application processing, scrutiny, data management, accessibility and the selection process.

Under the NOS Scheme, funds are released in advance through Letters of Authorization (LoA) to the concerned Indian Missions/Embassies with direction to disburse the requisite funds to concerned Universities and students at the earliest upon receipt of claims.

In Andhra Pradesh, 18 students have been awarded scholarships and enrolled abroad under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme during the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26. The number of beneficiaries was 4 in 2020-21, 3 in 2023-24, 3 in 2024-25 and 5 in 2025-26.

District-wise data for Andhra Pradesh shows that students from Chittoor received scholarships in 2020-21, 2023-24 and 2025-26. Beneficiaries were also recorded from Annamayya, Bapatla, Krishna, Palnadu, Prakasam, Visakhapatnam and Y.S.R. Kadapa districts during the period.

The Government's measures to expand awareness, digitise the application process and facilitate timely disbursement are aimed at improving access to overseas higher education opportunities for Scheduled Caste students.

2297832.title: From Financial Constraints to Engineering Aspirations: How Scholarship Support Helped MOHIT YADAV Continue His B.Tech Education
2297832.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to Engineering Aspirations: How Scholarship Support Helped MOHIT YADAV Continue His B.Tech Education
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

Access to quality education can play an important role in helping students pursue their aspirations and build better opportunities for the future. However, for students from middle-class families facing financial constraints, the expenses associated with higher education can become a significant challenge.

Demonstrating how scholarship assistance can provide relief to students facing economic challenges, Mr Mohit Yadav, a 19-year-old student belonging to the Other Backward Class (OBC) category, comes from a middle-class family and is pursuing a B.Tech in Civil Engineering. The expenses related to education, books, hostel and other academic requirements were difficult for his family to manage. Despite these challenges, Mohit remained focused on his studies and aspired to secure a good job and improve his family's financial condition through higher education and technical knowledge.

During the 2025–26 academic year, educational financial assistance of ₹1,59,400 was provided to Mohit. The support helped reduce the financial burden on his family and enabled him to continue his engineering education without interruption.

With the financial burden related to his educational expenses reduced, Mohit has been able to focus more on his academics and career preparation. He is currently pursuing his B.Tech in Civil Engineering and working towards strengthening his technical skills for future employment opportunities.

Expressing his feelings about the support from the Ministry, Mohit Yadav said,

Mohit Yadav's story highlights how timely scholarship assistance can provide meaningful support to students facing financial constraints. By helping ease the cost of education, the support has enabled him to continue his engineering studies and work towards his goal of securing a good job and contributing to the financial well-being of his family.

2297833.title: Central Government Disburses ₹19,216.46 Crore Under Various Scholarship Schemes for SC Students During Last Three Years
2297833.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Central Government Disburses ₹19,216.46 Crore Under Various Scholarship Schemes for SC Students During Last Three Years
Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students Accounts for ₹17,224.63 Crore; DBT and Regular Reviews Help Streamline Scholarship Disbursement
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has disbursed a total of ₹19,216.46 crore during the last three financial years towards various scholarship schemes for Scheduled Caste (SC) students administered by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

This information was provided by the Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar in a reply to Shri Raja A in the Lok Sabha today.

He said the total amount disbursed under these scholarship schemes increased from ₹6,094.48 crore in 2023-24 to ₹6,200.59 crore in 2024-25 and further to ₹6,921.39 crore in 2025-26.

The scholarship schemes covered include the Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students, Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs & Others, Top Class Education Scheme (TCS) and the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme for SC and other eligible candidates, he further said.

Dr Kumar said under the Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students, ₹17,224.63 crore was disbursed during the last three financial years. The amount released increased from ₹5,475.42 crore in 2023-24 to ₹5,562.26 crore in 2024-25 and ₹6,186.95 crore in 2025-26.

The Minister further said the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs & Others accounted for ₹1,469.92 crore during the three-year period, with ₹446.66 crore released in 2023-24, ₹460.90 crore in 2024-25 and ₹562.36 crore in 2025-26. Under the Top Class Education Scheme, ₹304.29 crore was released, while ₹217.62 crore was released under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme during the same period.

Under the Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students, Tamil Nadu received ₹713.70 crore in 2023-24, ₹1,032.09 crore in 2024-25 and ₹1,034.94 crore in 2025-26 as Central Assistance. Maharashtra received ₹1,652.98 crore, ₹929.92 crore and ₹1,095.80 crore respectively during the three years, while Uttar Pradesh received ₹674.83 crore, ₹366.02 crore and ₹617.64 crore respectively.

Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs & Others, Tamil Nadu received ₹70.56 crore in 2023-24, ₹109.45 crore in 2024-25 and ₹121.49 crore in 2025-26.

The Post Matric Scholarship for SCs and Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs & Others are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, under which the Department releases the Central share through the central portal after the respective States and Union Territories release their share. The National Overseas Scholarship and Top Class Education Scheme for SCs are Central Sector Schemes.

Under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme, funds are released in advance through a Letter of Authorisation (LoA) to Indian Missions, while funds under the Top Class Education Scheme are released directly to eligible students through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

The Minister stated that Department regularly reviews the scholarship schemes to address issues relating to delayed release of scholarships. Measures include capacity-building programmes, technical handholding, national-level Chintan Shivirs and workshops involving States, Union Territories and other stakeholders.

The Government has further stated that DBT into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries has streamlined payment processes and reduced delays.

Under the Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers for Scheduled Castes (SHREYAS-SCs), the Top Class Scholarship for SC Students is implemented as a Central Sector Scheme and, therefore, there is no State-wise or district-wise allocation. During the last three financial years, ₹304.29 crore was released under the scheme.

The Government continues to strengthen the implementation of scholarship schemes through digital payment mechanisms, regular reviews, technical support and capacity-building initiatives to facilitate timely release of scholarships to eligible SC students across the country.

2297830.title: Government Strengthens Rehabilitation Framework for Persons Engaged in Begging under SMILE-Beggary Scheme
2297830.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Rehabilitation Framework for Persons Engaged in Begging under SMILE-Beggary Scheme
₹45.59 Crore Released under SMILE-Beggary Scheme Since Inception; 10,446 Persons Including 2,824 Children Rehabilitated
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has taken comprehensive measures to strengthen the care, rehabilitation and social reintegration of persons engaged in begging through the Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) – Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging (SMILE-Beggary) Scheme.

This information was provided by the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma, in a written reply to Dr. M P Abdussamad Samdani in the Lok Sabha.

The reply said that since inception of the SMILE-Beggary Scheme on 23 October 2023 and up to 31 July 2026, a total of ₹45.59 crore has been released under the Scheme. This includes ₹40.04 crore released to implementing authorities/cities, with the balance utilised towards administrative and other scheme-related expenditure.

As on 31 July 2026, a total of 10,446 persons including 2,824 children, have been rehabilitated under the SMILE-Beggary Scheme. Of these, 7,622 are adult beneficiaries, the reply further said.

Children rescued under the Scheme are provided age-appropriate care, education, counselling and family reintegration and are therefore not covered under vocational training interventions.

The Scheme provides vocational training to eligible beneficiaries based on their aptitude, age, physical and mental condition, and local livelihood opportunities. Training includes trades and livelihood activities such as carpentry, tailoring, housekeeping, management of community toilets, sanitation services, hair cutting, security services, cooking, gardening, driving/operation of e-rickshaws and other locally relevant trades.

Beneficiaries are also facilitated in forming community/group-based Self-Help Groups and are linked with banks and other financial institutions for financial assistance to undertake self-employment and income-generating activities. These include tiffin stalls/food vending carts, vegetable vending carts and group-based enterprises such as preparation of spices, pickles, snacks and papads.

The written reply said as per the State/UT-wise details provided in the Lok Sabha reply, Tamil Nadu recorded the highest number of adult beneficiaries rehabilitated at 1,557, followed by Madhya Pradesh (1,135), Uttar Pradesh (884), Maharashtra (817), Assam (472), Andhra Pradesh (466), Jammu & Kashmir (434) and Kerala (418).

The Government's measures under the SMILE-Beggary Scheme aim to strengthen institutional mechanisms for care, rehabilitation, skill development, livelihood support and social reintegration, while ensuring dignified living conditions and effective monitoring of Beggars’/Shelter Homes.

In compliance with the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in M.S. Patter vs. State of NCT of Delhi (Civil Appeal No. 12216 of 2025), the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has developed Model Guidelines for Beggars’/Shelter Homes through a National Consultative Committee and extensive consultations with States and Union Territories. The Guidelines were circulated to all States/UTs on 13 April 2026 for necessary compliance and effective implementation.

The National Consultative Committee included representatives from the Ministries of Law & Justice, Health & Family Welfare, Housing and Urban Affairs, Women and Child Development, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, the National Human Rights Commission, State/UT Governments and non-governmental organisations working in the sector.

The Model Guidelines establish a comprehensive framework for humane, dignified and rights-based rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging. They prescribe minimum standards for infrastructure and capacity, preventive healthcare and sanitation, nutrition and food safety, vocational training and rehabilitation, legal aid and awareness, child and gender sensitivity, accountability, oversight, monitoring, implementation and compliance.

To facilitate identification, profiling and rehabilitation, the Ministry has developed a dedicated mobile application, with login credentials shared with implementing cities. The application facilitates a comprehensive survey of persons engaged in begging for their rehabilitation under the SMILE-Beggary Scheme.

The Model Guidelines further provide for establishment of a Digital Monitoring System by States/UTs to capture standardised information relating to admission of rescued persons/residents, health status, skill development and training, rehabilitation, release, follow-up and family reunion. The National Online Portal of the Ministry serves as a central repository of information relating to the SMILE-Beggary Scheme and facilitates real-time monitoring of implementation across States and Union Territories through periodic reporting and maintenance of scheme-related information.

Two-Yearly Infrastructure and Social Audits

The Model Guidelines mandate that every Beggar/Shelter Home undergo a third-party infrastructure and social audit at least once every two years. The audit covers structural safety, disability and age-friendliness, electrical systems, sanitation, water supply, and the safety and security of residents. The District Social Welfare Officer or designated authority is responsible for monitoring compliance and ensuring timely rectification of deficiencies identified during the audit. The Guidelines also prescribe minimum space standards for Beggars’/Shelter Homes to prevent overcrowding and ensure dignified living conditions.

2297824.title: CCRAS-CARI Inaugurates Extension OPD Facility in New Delhi
2297824.body_html:
AYUSH
CCRAS-CARI Inaugurates Extension OPD Facility in New Delhi
New Facility to Expand Access to Quality, Evidence-Based Ayurvedic Healthcare Services in the National Capital
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), New Delhi, under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Ministry of Ayush today inaugurated an Extension Outpatient Department (OPD) in New Delhi. The new facility is aimed at further strengthening the delivery of accessible, quality and evidence-based Ayurvedic healthcare services to the people of Rohini and adjoining areas.

Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS, inaugurated the facility in the presence of senior officers and dignitaries.

Addressing the gathering, Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya reiterated CCRAS’s commitment to expanding the reach of evidence-based Ayurveda and making quality Ayurvedic healthcare services more accessible to the public. He emphasised the importance of strengthening clinical services and extending the benefits of Ayurveda to communities through institutional and outreach initiatives.

Dr. Hemanta Panigrahi, Institute In-charge, CARI, delivered the welcome address, while Dr. N. Srikanth, Deputy Director General, CCRAS, highlighted the importance of expanding evidence-based Ayurvedic clinical services at the community level. Shri Deepak Kochhar, Deputy Director (Administration), CCRAS, and Shri M. Shivkumar Reddy, Superintendent Engineer, CPWD, spoke on the administrative and infrastructure aspects of the facility.

The new Extension OPD will provide accessible Ayurvedic outpatient services to residents of Rohini and adjoining areas, strengthening CARI, New Delhi’s clinical outreach and bringing evidence-based Ayurveda closer to the community.

The initiative is in line with the Ministry of Ayush’s continued efforts to strengthen the Ayush healthcare ecosystem, expand institutional healthcare infrastructure and make traditional systems of medicine more accessible to citizens. Such outreach facilities also support the broader objective of integrating evidence-based practices of Ayurveda into accessible and community-oriented healthcare delivery.

The inauguration marks another step towards strengthening the network of Ayurvedic clinical services in the National Capital and advancing the vision of accessible, quality and evidence-based Ayush healthcare for all.

Extension OPD Facility Address: FC-5, Block-A, Sector-28, Rohini, New Delhi.

GeM has started utilising AI/ML based analytical models to identify suspicious procurement patterns, including potential buyer-seller collusion, abnormal pricing and repeated participation patterns. 2297818.title: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan Enables Integrated and Coordinated Infrastructure Planning
2297818.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
PM GatiShakti National Master Plan Enables Integrated and Coordinated Infrastructure Planning
PM GatiShakti Provides Integrated Planning Framework without Separate Budgetary Provisions
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched in October 2021, is a transformative “Whole of Government” approach to bring together various Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs to ensure integrated planning and coordinated execution of infrastructure projects. PMGS NMP aims to facilitate Ministries/States in data driven decision making by utilizing geospatial data, satellite imagery and API integration to monitor, plan, and optimize infrastructure development. The PMGS NMP is facilitating Ministries/States in planning of their respective infrastructure projects, including social infrastructure projects, in integrated, synchronized and coordinated manner to provide seamless and efficient connectivity for the movement of people, goods, and services across various modes of transport, thereby enhancing last-mile connectivity and reducing travel time.

PM GatiShakti provides an integrated planning framework; the approval and implementation of the projects are undertaken by the respective central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs under their plans, schemes, procedures and budgetary/funding provisions. Hence, no quantified targets or expenditure requirements have been set under PM GatiShakti initiative.

The Network Planning Group (NPG), constituted under the PM GatiShakti framework, evaluates the critical infrastructure projects of the central Government to ensure integrated planning, multimodality, inter-modality, synchronization of efforts, last mile connectivity, comprehensive development in and around the project location, data driven decision makings, etc at the planning stage. As on date, 396 infrastructure projects with total estimated cost of about ₹ 18.66 Lakh Crore have been evaluated through the NPG mechanism. Out of these 396 projects, 256 projects have been sanctioned - out of which, 198 projects are under implementation. Ministry-wise details are given at Annexure-A.

Government carries out assessment of its initiatives/schemes from time to time through various studies, surveys, etc. Apart from these, there are several studies by universities and research scholars in this respect. As per these assessments, the integrated planning initiatives like, PM GatiShakti, National Logistics Policy, PRAGATI, Sagarmala, development of connectivity infrastructure (expressways/ national highways/ dedicated rail freight corridors and rail tracks, industrial corridors/hubs), etc. have shaped the vision of connected and competitive India and have improved logistics efficiency, turn-around time, ease of doing business, industrial growth and reduced logistics cost in country. An assessment of logistic cost has been carried out by DPIIT in the year 2025 in collaboration with National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER). As per the assessment, the logistics cost in India is estimated at 7.9% of the GDP, which is at par with the advanced economies in the world. The Economic Survey 2023-24 highlighted that these measures have improved domestic manufacturing and export competitiveness. A study by Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore on impact of development of National Highway projects underlines that every-one rupee expenditure in National Highways development leads to a ₹3.2 increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

So far 58 Central Ministries/Departments and all 36 States/UTs have been onboarded on the PMGS NMP, covering all infrastructure sectors like road, rail, ports & waterways, power, petroleum & natural gas, civil aviation, telecommunications, industrial corridors, etc. Further, PM GatiShakti public platform (url: ugi.pmgatishakti.gov.in) has been launched in September 2025, which provided access of PM GatiShakti data analytics to private entities and general public. Through this Query based mechanism, public and private entities are able to plan their projects by obtaining data analytic reports from the PMGS-NMP Portal through a simple query-based mechanism. The States have been encouraged to expand the use of PM GatiShakti for district level planning. About 1800 data layers have been integrated and over 65 software modules/tools and more than 100 mobile/web applications have been developed and integrated on the platform for the use of stakeholders. Further expansion of the PM GatiShakti initiative is a continuous process - mapping/integration of more data layers, development and integration of additional features, software modules/tools for planning and analysis modules/tools, mobile/ web applications, etc. to be continue further as per the requirements of the Ministries/Departments, States/UTs and other stakeholders.

This information was given by Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297792.title: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
2297792.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

Reforms for a Growing MSME Sector

The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed by the Parliament in August 2026. It updates the existing MSMED Act, 2006 to align its provisions with the requirements of the MSME sector. The amendments seek to reduce payment-related constraints, make dispute resolution more time-bound and simplify compliance. Their broader objective is to facilitate the growth, development and competitiveness of MSMEs while promoting Ease of Doing Business.

 

Introduction

The MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was passed by the Parliament in August 2026. The importance of this amendment stems from the sector’s growing role in India’s economy. The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act (MSMED Act) was notified in 2006. Since then, the MSME ecosystem has expanded in scale, diversity and digital reach.

According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, MSMEs account for 31.1% of GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing output and 48.58% of exports.   As on August 2026, 9.16 crore MSMEs are registered on the Udyam platform, employing more than 40 crore people.  Technological advances and IT-enabled systems have further transformed the MSME landscape.  These enterprises now operate across rural, semi-urban and urban areas and participate more actively in formal supply chains.

The MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 builds on this foundation. It aims to align the legal framework with the sector’s changing needs and its growing economic significance.

 Changes introduced in the Bill

The 2026 Bill revises certain specific provisions under the MSMED Act, 2006. Details of key areas of reform are highlighted below:

Areas of Reform

The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006

The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026

MSME Classification

MSMEs are classified on the basis of prescribed investment thresholds for:

  1. plant and machinery in manufacturing; and
  2. equipment in services.

MSMEs are classified on the basis of:

  1. investment in plant and machinery or equipment; and
  2. turnover.

 

MSME Registration

Medium enterprises engaged in manufacturing are required to file a memorandum with specified authority. Filing of memorandum is voluntary for other MSMEs.

 

The Bill makes filing of the memorandum free and voluntary for all MSMEs.

The Central Government shall notify a national platform for the purpose. State governments may also notify State digital platforms.

State scheme benefits may be extended to MSMEs registered on the national and state-level platform.

Payments through Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS)

Addressed through introduction of a new provision in the Bill.

All Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) are required to settle invoices for goods and services procured from MSMEs through the TReDS platform. This aims to address payment-related issues faced by MSMEs.

States may mandate their Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs), authorities, or entities to use TReDS for invoice settlement.

Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs) Framework

State Governments may establish one or more MSE Facilitation Councils.

State Governments can establish multiple MSEFCs to enable faster resolution of payment-related disputes. They are also empowered to provide adequate infrastructure and resources, including physical infrastructure, digital systems and trained manpower, as may be necessary.

Mediation and Arbitration

The MSEFCs or referred mediation service providers are authorised to settle payment disputes by mediation.

Where a mediation is not successful, the dispute may be referred for arbitration.

Central Government may establish an online mechanism for conducting online mediation or arbitration.

Specific timelines have been introduced for mediation and arbitration:

  1. The MSEFC or mediation service provider must complete mediation within 90 days from the date fixed for the first appearance.
  2. If mediation is terminated, the MSEFC are required to refer the matter for arbitration within 30 days.
  3. The MSEFC or an institution or centre providing alternative dispute resolution services must make the arbitral  award within 90 days from the completion of pleadings.

Dispute Resolution

Application to set aside a Council’s order/ award may be filed in court after depositing 75% of the awarded amount.

The Bill also allows such applications. While the application is pending, the court may direct that a reasonable portion of the deposited amount be paid to the MSME supplier.

Courts shall direct payment to MSE suppliers when an application to set aside a decree, award or order remains pending for more than six months. The payment must be at least 50% of the awarded amount.

Recovery of Dues

Addressed through introduction of a new provision in the Bill.

Mediated settlement agreement or arbitral award can be recovered as ‘arrears of land revenue’. This applies to agreements or awards made under Section 18 by the Facilitation Council, a mediation service provider or an alternative dispute resolution institution.

Recovery may be undertaken through the District Collector, Deputy Commissioner or another notified authority. The notified authority must have jurisdiction over the location of the buyer’s assets.

Decriminalisation of Offences

Wilfully providing false registration information attracts a fine of up to ₹1,000 for the first conviction and ₹1,000-₹10,000 for subsequent convictions.

Failure to report unpaid dues to MSME suppliers in annual accounts attracts a fine of at least ₹10,000.

Non-filing of registration or non-supply of information: Earlier, these violations attracted conviction and a fine. The penal provisions have now been decriminalised.

Furnishing incorrect information: A warning will be issued for the first instance, followed by a penalty for the second and subsequent instances.

Non-disclosure of unpaid dues by buyers: It now attracts a warning for the first instance, a penalty for the second and a fine for the third and subsequent instances.

Digital and Institutional Support

The reforms introduced by the Bill are supported by digital platforms and institutional mechanisms established across the MSME ecosystem.

Expanding Formal Recognition: The Udyam Registration Portal gives MSMEs official recognition through a free, paperless and self-declaration-based online process.  The Udyam Assist Platform complements this initiative by formally recognising informal micro enterprises. This includes enterprises without GST registration or coverage under the Income Tax system, based on data verified by authorised partners.

Improving Access to Financing: TReDS is an electronic platform that enables MSMEs to finance or discount trade receivables. It operates in accordance with guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India.  The value of invoices discounted through the platform rose from ₹40,000 crore in 2022-23 to ₹3.47 lakh crore in 2025-26.  

Enabling Online Dispute Resolution (ODR): The ODR Portal was launched in June 2025. It offers MSEs a low-cost, end-to-end digital mechanism for resolving delayed payment disputes, including small-value claims.

Strengthening the MSEFC Network: 161 MSEFCs have been established across States and Union Territories. MSEFCs are set up to adjudicate disputes arising from payment delays faced by Micro and Small Enterprises.

Conclusion

The MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks to strengthen the foundations of an MSME’s journey from a small enterprise to a growing business. It provides for a stronger regulatory framework to help MSMEs operate and expand in an evolving business environment.

2297790.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DDU-GKY
2297790.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
IMPLEMENTATION OF DDU-GKY
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is one of the cluster of initiatives under DeenDayalAntyodayaYojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement-linked skilling programs. To align with evolving industry requirements and emerging employment opportunities, revised guidelines under DDU-GKY 2.0 have been rolled out from FY 2025-26 with focus on industry-led training, sustainable employment, enhanced post-placement support, upskilling and reskilling opportunities and greater flexibility in training delivery. Emerging sectors such as Electric Vehicle (EV) maintenance, renewable energy, logistics, healthcare, care economy, retail, hospitality and media & entertainment are also being prioritised. Since inception, around 18.45 lakh rural youth have been trained and about 12.35 lakh candidates have been placed under the scheme.

 

Training under DDU-GKY has been imparted across diverse sectors including Apparel, Automotive, Beauty & Wellness, Construction, Electronics, Healthcare, Hospitality, IT-ITES, Logistics, Retail, Telecom, Agriculture and allied sectors, among others. Placement of trained candidates is facilitated through mandatory industry partnerships, employer tie-ups, job fairs, campus placement drives, industry consultations, and engagement with Sector Skill Councils and employers. The scheme mandates placement-linked outcomes and continuous industry participation in curriculum design and training delivery. Further, the features like 20% allocation of targets to captive employers in each State/UT and the batch mode payments to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) linked to successful mandatory placement period of 6 months, have been incorporated to ensure coordination with industries.

 

To improve retention and sustainability of employment, DDU-GKY 2.0 emphasizes long-term employment outcomes (minimum 70% placement including maximum 20% self or gig employment for minimum of 6 months) through one year post-placement tracking and support, counselling, migration support, alumni engagement, grievance redressal mechanisms, and opportunities for upskilling/reskilling. Under the revised framework, candidates are required to be tracked and supported for a longer duration to facilitate sustained employment and career progression. Since inception, about 12.35 lakh candidates have been placed under the Scheme.

 

For FY 2026-27, Budget Estimates (BE) of ₹750 crore has been kept for training around 1.37 lakh rural youth. Further, Mother Sanction amounting ₹361.96 crore has been issued to the States/UTs and an expenditure of ₹50.89 crore has been made by the States/UTs till date.

 

In the State of Madhya Pradesh, DDU-GKY is being implemented through the Madhya Pradesh State Rural Livelihoods Mission (MPSRLM). Since inception, around 93 thousand candidates have been trained and around 56 thousand candidates have been placed in the State of Madhya Pradesh under the scheme. Further, for FY 2026-27, mother sanction amounting to ₹10.00 crore has been issued to the State of Madhya Pradesh.

2297784.title: TARGET AND STATUS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE UNDER PMAY-G
2297784.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
TARGET AND STATUS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE UNDER PMAY-G
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

Under Pradhan MantriAwaasYojana- Gramin, a total of 32.47 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 26.57 lakh houses have been completed duringFY2025-26, inclusive of sanctions issued in previous financial years. The State/UT-wise details areprovidedatAnnexure - I.

 

As on 03.08.2026, against the total target of 4.18 crore houses allocated to the States/UTs under PMAY-G, 3.91 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.12 crore houses have been completed. The remaining 79 lakh sanctioned houses are under construction.

Under PMAY-G, the house is constructed by the beneficiary himself/herself or under his/her supervision. Further, as per the guidelines of PMAY-G, the States/UTs provide the beneficiaries a bouquet of options of house designs according to the local climatic conditions, using appropriate local material and technology suitable to the region of their residence. The State/UT Government can also facilitate supply of construction material at competitive rates. The Ministry of Rural Development has published a compendium of rural housing typologies “PAHAL” which is available on the program website of PMAY-G. This can be accessed through AwaasApp. Further, to ensure good quality construction of houses under PMAY-G, the Government of India has rolled out Rural Mason Training (RMT) Program with the target to train adequate number of masons for house construction in rural areas.

 

A number of steps have been taken by the Ministry to ensure timely construction of houses in all States/UTs under PMAY-G. These include:

 

(i) Timely allocation of targets to the States/UTs and release of adequate funds;

(ii) Regular review of progress;

(iii) Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a Dashboard;

(iv) Regular Workshops are conducted by the Ministry with the States/UTs;

(v) Rural Mason Training program, etc.

 

In addition to the unit assistance provided under the scheme, PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water through convergence with the JalJeevan Mission (JJM) and HarGharNal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connections through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan MantriUjjwalaYojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas or other relevant schemes.

 

As per the scheme guidelines, up to 5% of the targets under PMAY-G, are reserved for Special Projects. E.g. for Rehabilitation / relocation of families whose houses have been completely /substantially damaged on account of Natural hazards as categorized in the extant National Disaster Management Plan of National Disaster Management Authority - Flood, earthquake, fire, etc.

 

Further, under PMAY-G, a minimum 60% of the target at the national level is earmarked for both Scheduled Caste (SC)/Schedules Tribes (ST) households subject to availability of such eligible beneficiaries.

 

Additionally, under Pradhan MantriJanjatiAdivasiNyayaMahaAbhiyan (PM-JANMAN) of Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the provision providing pucca houses to the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) households with basic amenities is one of the interventions being implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

The funds under PMAY-G are allocated to States/UTs, with each State/UT treated as a single unit. The distribution of these funds among districts is undertaken by the respective State/UT Governments. Over the last two financial years, expenditure under Special Projects stood at ₹528.04 crore, while Aspirational Districts recorded spending of ₹17,281.58 crore, inclusive of both Central and State shares. Further, under PM-JANMAN, a Central share of ₹2,465.38 crore was released for PVTG beneficiaries during FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26, against which a total expenditure of ₹6,329.06 crore was incurred, comprising contributions from both the Centre and the States.

2297780.title: INTEGRATED MASTER PLAN FOR RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE
2297780.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
INTEGRATED MASTER PLAN FOR RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

Under its broad policy framework, Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) has been undertaking various targeted interventions for integrated and sustainable development rural areas of the country. With the main focus on infrastructure development, increasing livelihood opportunities, empowering rural women and expanding livelihood opportunities, MoRD is implementing Pradhan Mantri Gram SadakYojana(PMGSY), Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar&Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) and DeendayalAntyodayaYojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) across the country including Bhind and Datia districts of Madhya Pradesh. As per the implementation framework of the programmes, States/UTs are conceiving the project proposals for infrastructure including roads and sustainable assets, identification of beneficiary, generation of demand for employment, livelihood programmes, keeping in view the actual requirement of interventions for improving the quality of life of rural population. The above programmes are implemented in convergence with various central and state schemes to optimize the pace of rural development in the country. However, at present, there is no proposal in this Ministry for an integrated master plan for rural infrastructure and livelihood development for each LokSabha Constituency.

MoRD has evolved a comprehensive multilevel and multi format system of periodic assessment and review of progress and outcome of its rural development schemes, through Performance Review Committee Meetings, National Level Monitors (NLMs), Area Officers Schemes, Common Review Mission, Mid-Term Review, Labour Budget meetings, Labour Budget Revision meetings, Programme Review meetings, Concurrent Evaluation and Impact Assessment Studies. Specific reviews of States/UTs are also undertaken from time to time and action is taken on the basis of their findings. In addition, MoRD constitutes District Level Development Coordination and Monitoring Committees (DISHA) under the chairpersonship of the respective Members of Parliament to foster better coordination among elected representatives of Parliament, State Legislatures, and Local Governments (Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies) to ensure the effective and timely implementation of key Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes including the schemes/programmes of MoRD at district level.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297777.title: STUDY ON MIGRATION
2297777.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
STUDY ON MIGRATION
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) does not maintain data pertaining to migration prone areas or migration trends. However, with a view to inter alia address issues of migration of rural people, the Government has adopted a multi-dimensional course of action such as, provision of improved infrastructural facilities (i.e; roads, drinking water supply, housing, sanitation and connectivity), equitable dispersal of resources to remove regional disparities, employment generation, imparting of skills, encouraging entrepreneurial activity and providing easy access to financial assistance & credit facilities etc.

 

In this direction, Ministry of Rural Development(MoRD) is implementing various rural development schemes/programmes such as Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Pradhan Mantri AwaasYojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), Pradhan Mantri Gram SadakYojana (PMGSY), DeendayalAntyodayaYojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), DeenDayalUpadhyayaGrameenKaushalyaYojana (DDUGKY), Rural Self Employment Training Institutes(RSETIs), National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) and Watershed Development Component (WDC) of the Pradhan MantriKrishiSinchayeeYojana (WDC-PMKSY) for overall development of rural areas of the country.

 

The Government undertakes regular assessment and reviews of the progress of implementation of rural development programmes towards ensuring effective achievement of defined objectives. Details of persondays generated, Self Help Groups (SHGs) formed and houses completed under MGNREGS, DAY-NRLM and PMAY-G respectively are given below: -

 

Name of programme

Major benefit accrued

Since inception of programme in 2006, a total of 4994.17 crorepersondays have been generated as on 30.06.2026

DAY-NRLM

The programme launched in 2011 has mobilized a total of 10.08 crore women into 92 lakhs Self Help Groups as on 30.06.2026

PMAY-G

A total of 3.11 crore houses have been completed since 2016 to till present

The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026, provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment to every willing rural household and focuses on creation of durable assets and strengthening sustainable rural livelihoods. The Programme includes a dedicated thematic area on Livelihood Infrastructure, covering agriculture and allied activities, rural enterprises, Self Help Groups and other income-generating activities, thereby creating and strengthening sustainable livelihood opportunities in rural areas. Further, works under Water Security, including water conservation, watershed development, groundwater recharge and source sustainability, support agricultural activities by improving the availability and sustainability of water resources, thereby contributing to enhanced agricultural productivity and rural livelihoods.

Similarly, works under Mitigation of Extreme Weather Events and Disaster Preparedness, including measures for drought, floods and other extreme weather events, help protect agricultural and rural livelihood assets and strengthen the resilience of rural communities. Thus, the combined focus on livelihood infrastructure, water security, climate resilience and rural infrastructure is intended to enhance rural employment opportunities, strengthen agricultural and allied livelihoods and promote sustainable rural development. These provisions are applicable across all rural areas of the country, including JalgaonLokSabha Constituency in Maharashtra, and are aimed at strengthening livelihoods and reducing vulnerability to seasonal and climate-related livelihood distress.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297771.title: REVISED TARGET FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSES UNDER PMAY-G
2297771.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
REVISED TARGET FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSES UNDER PMAY-G
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi

During the last five financial years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26), a total target of 2.13 crore houses has been allocated to the States/UTs under PMAY-G. Against this, 1.95 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 1.21 crore houses have been constructed. The State/UT-wise details of targets allocated, houses sanctioned, houses constructed and houses under construction are provided in Annexure-I.

 

During the last five financial years, a total Central share of Rs. 1,31,100.02crore has been released to the States/UTs by the Ministry, while Rs. 2,17,896.40 crore (including both Central and State share) has been spent under the scheme. The State/UT-wise details of Central share released by the Ministry and utilization during the last five financial years by is provided in Annexure-II.

 

The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing the Pradhan MantriAwaasYojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) w.e.f. 1st April 2016 to provide assistance to eligible rural households for the construction of Pucca houses with basic amenities to achieve the objective of "Housing For All" in rural areas. The scheme seeks to provide assistance for the construction of 4.95 crore houses by 31.03.2029. At present, a target of 4.18 crorehouseshas been allocated to the States and UTs, and State/UT wise number is given in Annexure- III.

 

The release of PMAY-G funds had withheld/delayed in certain cases where serious irregularities in implementation were reported and satisfactory corrective action was not established.

 

In the case of Odisha, complaints alleging irregularities in the implementation of PMAY-G were verified through inquiries by the State Government and Central Teams deputed by the Ministry. The inquiries revealed deficiencies relating to beneficiary selection, construction quality, inspections, branding of PMAY-G houses and compliance with scheme guidelines. Accordingly, the State Government was directed to take corrective and disciplinary action and submit an Action Taken Report (ATR). Since the ATR initially submitted by the State was not found satisfactory, the release of subsequent instalments of Central assistance was withheld pending satisfactory compliance. The State Government has since taken the required corrective and disciplinary measures and submitted a satisfactory ATR. Accordingly, the release of PMAY-G funds to the State has been resumed.

 

In the case of West Bengal, following the allocation of targets from the finalized Awaas+ 2018 survey lists in November 2022, complaints regarding irregularities in the implementation of PMAY-G were received. These complaints were verified through National Level Monitoring (NLM) teams and Senior Officers Teams following which release of Central share of funds was withheld from FY 2022-23 onwards. The ATR submitted by the State is currently under examination.

2297764.title: RURAL SCHEMES IMPLEMENTED FOR SHGS
2297764.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
RURAL SCHEMES IMPLEMENTED FOR SHGS
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing DeendayalAntyodayaYojana -National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) with the objective of organizing the rural households into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and continuously nurturing and supporting them till they attain appreciable increase in income over a period of time and improve their quality of life. Cumulatively, 10.08 crore women have been mobilized into 92.30 lakh SHGs. The mission seeks to achieve its objective through investing in four core components, viz., (1) social mobilization, promotion and strengthening of self-managed and financially sustainable community institutions of the rural poor; (2) financial inclusion of the rural poor; (3) sustainable livelihoods; and (4) social inclusion & social development. The Mission is implemented across the country in 28 States and 6 UTs (except Delhi & Chandigarh).

 

The Ministry facilitates access to institutional credit for women SHGs under DAY-NRLM. Under the programme, women SHGs avail collateral-free loans from Scheduled Commercial Banks and Cooperative Banks in accordance with guidelines of the Reserve Bank of India and National Bank for Agriculture & Rural Development (NABARD). For Training of these SHGs, Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) provide skill development and entrepreneurship training to rural youth including these SHGs with a strong focus on empowering women. These institute promote self-employment by supporting livelihood and enterprise development, facilitating bank credit linkages, and providing comprehensive post-training handholding.

 

Further, Community Managed Training Centres (CMTCs) are promoted under the DAY-NRLM which are community-owned and community-managed institutions that serve as hubs for capacity building, peer learning, and knowledge exchange.

 

The total number of women SHGs under DAY-NRLM set up in the country, state-wise is given at Annexure-I.

 

Self-Help Groups (SHGs) face several key challenges, including social barriers such as gender inequality, migration, and low literacy further hinder participation and inclusion. Additionally, expansion of marketing facilities, limited access to technology, and vulnerability to natural disasters, health emergencies, climate change, and economic downturns also exist.

 

Under DAY-NRLM, the Ministry of Rural Development has adopted a multipronged strategy for the social, economic, and institutional empowerment of rural women. The positive outcomes of these interventions have been validated through independent impact evaluation studies commissioned by the Ministry. The 3ie Impact Evaluation Study (2025), based on two rounds of data collection conducted in 2019 and 2024 across 9 States, covering about 23,000 households, found that household incomes increased by 9.5% in NRLM blocks, while income gains in mature community institution clusters ranged from 12% to 33%. The study also reported an increase of 6–11% in per capita household consumption, along with improvements in women’s empowerment, livelihood diversification, and overall household welfare.

 

Also, NITI Aayog’s Evaluation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the Rural Development Sector (2025) assessed DAY-NRLM as a highly relevant and impactful programme, noting its contribution to increased incomes, diversified livelihood opportunities, enhanced financial inclusion and literacy, greater self-confidence among women, and improved social inclusion through strong community institutions and convergence with other development initiatives. These findings underscore the significant role of DAY-NRLM in advancing women’s empowerment and improving the socio-economic well-being of rural households. It has demonstrated significant positive outcomes, with average household incomes increasing by 49%. It has also contributed to women's economic and social empowerment, as 58% of women reported enhanced confidence, 52% experienced improved access to income-generating opportunities, and 46% became capable of managing their banking transactions independently. In addition, women-led enterprises have diversified into a range of livelihood activities, including tailoring, goat rearing, and agri-trading, thereby strengthening income sources and promoting sustainable rural livelihoods.

 

Further, the LakhpatiDidi Initiative is a program under the DAY-NRLM scheme aimed at enhancing the income of women Self-Help Group (SHG) members, with the goal of making them "LakhpatiDidi." It focuses on helping SHG members achieve an annual income of Rs. 1 lakh or more. The total count of LakhpatiDidis across the country has reached 3.46 crore, which shows the impact of DAY-NRLM scheme on the income of women members of SHGs.

2297747.title: Strengthening of Cooperative Institutions in Vellore
2297747.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
Strengthening of Cooperative Institutions in Vellore
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

To examine the functioning of cooperative institutions across the country, including those in Vellore district of Tamil Nadu, the Ministry of Cooperation (MoC) has adopted a multi-layered institutional mechanism for monitoring cooperative sector initiatives at the State and district levels, with a view to ensuring effective coordination, implementation and monitoring. For this purpose, committees have been constituted at various levels, from the national level to the district level. These include:

i. Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) – Chaired by the Hon’ble Minister of Home Affairs & Cooperation;

ii. National Level Coordination Committee (NLCC) – Chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation;

iii. State Cooperative Development Committee (SCDC) – Chaired by the Chief Secretary of the respective State/UT; and

iv. District Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC) – Chaired by the District Collector of the respective district.

As per information received from the State of Tamil Nadu, two SCDC meetings and two DCDC meetings have been convened so far.

Further, Ministry has launched the ‘Cooperative Ranking Framework’ which provides standardized parameters—including audit compliance, financial performance, and operational activities—that enable the State Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) to conduct independent assessments and take necessary steps to strengthen societies at the State, district, and block levels.

The sector-wise details of the total number and the number of functional cooperative societies in Vellore district are attached at Annexure-A.

The Government has undertaken a series of digital, financial and capacity-building measures to strengthen governance, professional management, service delivery, operational efficiency and outreach of cooperative institutions, including those functioning in Vellore district:

  • Under the National Plan for formation of new Multipurpose PACS, Dairy and Fishery Cooperative Societies to achieve cooperative coverage in every uncovered Panchayat/village over a period of five years, as on 15.07.2026, a 27 PACS, 940 DCS and 36 FCS have been registered in the State of Tamil Nadu including 11 DCS in the Vellore district.
  • Under the Central Sector Project for Computerization of PACS, 4,561 PACS have been sanctioned and Rs 55.73 Cr have been disbursed to the State of Tamil Nadu. As on 15.07.2026, hardware has been delivered to 4,532 PACS and 4,481 PACS have been onboarded onto the common ERP-based national software including 64 PACS in Vellore District. The initiative is aimed at improving transparency, accounting, audit, monitoring, digital service delivery and integration with the cooperative banking structure.
  • The Model Bye-laws circulated by the Ministry of Cooperation and adopted by the State enable PACS to undertake more than 25 diversified business activities.
  • As per information provided by the State of Tamil Nadu, in Vellore district, 55 PACS are functioning as Common Service Centres and Fair Price Shops; 43 PACS are providing micro-ATM facilities, 55 PACS are working as PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras.
  • Further, 28 PACS are providing agricultural machinery services, 9 are operating Pharmacy/Medical Store, one is operating a Cooperative Medical Shop, 43 PACS have godowns.
  • For improving professional management and long-term institutional sustainability, capacity-building programmes are conducted through the National Council for Cooperative Training. In Tamil Nadu, such programmes are implemented through the Natesan Institute of Cooperative Management, Chennai, and the Institute of Cooperative Management, Madurai. During the last five years, these institutions have trained 1,31,499 participants in the State, including 2,688 participants from Vellore district, in areas such as cooperative governance, financial management, digital literacy, computerization and business diversification.
  • In addition, 4,097 PACS Secretaries in Tamil Nadu have been trained in the effective use of Common Service Centre services; 4 programmes conducted for capacity building of 105 BoDs / Secretaries of M-PACS with emphasis on good governance, professional management, business diversification and effective functioning of societies.
  • Village-level awareness programmes are being conducted to disseminate information regarding Government schemes, institutional credit, market linkages and business diversification. In Tamil Nadu, 560 such programmes have benefited 72,885 members, including 2,234 members from Vellore district.
  • NABARD has conducted various cooperative training programmes covering key areas such as women empowerment for PACS staff, preparation of Business Development Plans, the impact of NPAs on the financial health of PACS, and corporate governance in PACS. During FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, a total of 578 such cooperative training programmes were conducted in Tamil Nadu, including Vellore, training 15,635 officials.
  • Financial and technical assistance is also available through the National Cooperative Development Corporation for eligible cooperative projects in agriculture, dairy, fisheries, handloom, marketing, processing, storage and allied sectors, subject to prescribed eligibility conditions and project appraisal. The details of financial assistance in the State of Tamil Nadu during last five years by NCDC is provided at Annexure-B

2297743.title: PRECISION AGRICULTURE
2297743.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
PRECISION AGRICULTURE
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has taken up a program of National Importance namely, Network Program on Precision Agriculture (ICAR - NePPA) having 16 ICAR Research Institutes of different domains. Under this program, technologies are developed using sensors, remote sensing at different platforms (ground, airborne -Drone and satellite platforms), AI and ICTs in line with international best practices in precision agriculture related to

  • Spatio-temporal monitoring and management of crop and soil health.
  • Sensor based post-harvest quality monitoring and management (of mango, banana, pulse and rice, etc).
  • IoT based precision vertical farming for high valued vegetables under controlled environment.
  • Developed sensor-based monitoring and management of aquatic environment for precision aquaculture.
  • Monitoring of livestock health using different IoT enabled sensing for precision livestock.

ICAR continuously studies, adapts and develops advanced precision agriculture and efficient land-use technologies suited to Indian conditions. ICAR Institutes have developed and validated technologies such as sensor-based irrigation, IoT-enabled environmental monitoring, drone-based spraying, AI-enabled precision planters, remote sensing and GIS applications, drip fertigation, poly-mulching, raised-bed cultivation, modified raised and sunken conservation beds, agro-aqua land configuration, automated livestock management systems, low-cost protected cultivation, hydroponics, aeroponics, agrivoltaic farming, precision subsurface drip irrigation and other water-efficient irrigation technologies to improve productivity, resource-use efficiency and sustainability in smallholder farming systems. ICAR has developed and demonstrated a tank-based super-intensive precision shrimp farming system. The technology yields 120–150 tonnes/ha/year over three annual cycles and the system integrate smart automation, strict biosecurity, and eco-efficient management for all farm sizes.

ICAR is promoting precision agriculture through:

  • Development and validation of AI-, IoT- and ICT-enabled decision support systems for crop and natural resource management;
  • Use of drones for crop monitoring, precision input application and crop health assessment;
  • Remote sensing, GIS and satellite-based monitoring for crop assessment and resource mapping;
  • Sensor and IoT-based irrigation and fertigation systems for efficient water and nutrient management;
  • Precision nutrient management using enhanced-efficiency fertilizers, nano-fertilizers and biofertilizers;
  • Development of digital tools such as the Dweep Microclimate Monitor and AI-based models for water stress assessment and livestock management;
  • Establishment of a Remote Pilot Training Organisation (RPTO) at Dehradun for UAV/drone training;
  • Technology demonstrations, farmer training, capacity building and digital advisory services through ICAR Institutes, AICRPs and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs).
  • AI, sensor and IoT based technologies/equipment/ systems developed for production and post production agriculture such as; smart micro-irrigation system utilizing automation and sensor networks to optimize water use efficiency,  Variable rate fertilizers applicator,  AI & IoT enable jute grading system,  SPAD meter 2.0 for measuring leaf chlorophyll concentration, IoT System for Monitoring and Control of Cold Room, Instrument for Rapid detection of Aflatoxin-B1 in maize, Smart Banana Supply Chain: Sensor based monitoring and Bloc-chain enabled Traceability, Digital twin-based fruit quality monitoring, AI based Grain Analyzer Software, Artificial Intelligence Based Quality Assessment of Rice Seeds, Contamination Measurement Techniques using Image Processing in Seed Cotton,  portable device for non-destructive and quick ginning percentage measurement based on computer vision and

machine learning etc. and conducted drone demonstrations in an area of 230 ha, benefitting 2487 farmers.

  • ICAR institutes use drones and mobile apps to demonstrate AI-driven fertilizer and pesticide spraying in some crops to farmers.

            In addition, some of the areas in which ICAR applies artificial intelligence (AI) are:           

  • Use of drone for collecting water samples for analysis from open-water bodies & difficult terrains; distribution of feed & medicines to the culture systems; transportation of fish & goods; biomass estimation; health monitoring, etc. 
  • Developed IoT-based dissolved oxygen management system.
  • Fisheries resource assessment and predictions in inland open-water under AI and Big Data platform.
  • Establishing smart production system and hatchery using automated devices and gadgets for enhancing production.
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, drones, and satellite imagery—to strengthen early disease warning systems, biosecurity, and overall livestock management. The specific initiatives and technical applications deployed for livestock protection.
  • Satellite & AI-Based Early Warning Systems: ICAR-National Institute of Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease Informatics (NIVEDI) utilizes Geographic Information Systems (GIS), satellite spatial datasets, and predictive machine learning models to forecast 15 economically important livestock diseases outbreaks up to two months in advance, enabling state authorities and farmers to take preventive action.
  • Sensor-Based Health & Reproduction Monitoring: Wearable IoT sensors (such as smart neck collars, rumination tags, and leg pedometers) are integrated into herd management systems to measure real-time body temperature, rumination activity, and estrus cycles, allowing early diagnosis of illness before clinical symptoms surface.
  • Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) scheme to promote adoption of new technologies in agriculture and allied sectors including agri-drones through technology assessment, demonstration and capacity development among the farmers. The KVKs/ICAR Institutes/Agricultural Universities conducted 38,402 Agri-drone demonstrations on nutrients, fertilizers, chemicals (insect & pest) applications in 41,280 ha area. Total 4,54,083 farmers participated in the Agri-Drone demonstrations and field interventions.    

ICAR promotes an integrated precision farming ecosystem by developing location-specific technologies for precision irrigation, nutrient management, protected cultivation, mechanization, digital decision support and climate-smart agriculture. These technologies are being disseminated through field demonstrations, farmer training, capacity building programmes and collaboration with State Departments, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and other stakeholders to facilitate their adoption by farmers.

Precision agriculture technologies have demonstrated significant improvements in productivity, profitability, resource-use efficiency and climate resilience. Precision irrigation technologies, including solar-powered Jhola Kundi systems, farm ponds and micro-irrigation, increased cropping intensity from 137% to 272%, doubled the crop diversification index (0.40 to 0.80), increased average monthly farmer income from ₹4,644 to ₹19,676, and reduced dependence on diesel and electricity while mitigating about 40.5 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually.At Goa, precision agriculture technologies increased rice and cowpea yields by 4.69% and 6.58%, respectively, while reducing irrigation water use by 92.9% and labour requirement by about 95%.  Farm pond-based rainwater harvesting systems increased crop yields by 20–55%, while polyhouse cultivation integrated with automated drip irrigation and fertigation generated net returns of ₹2.72 lakh per 15 gunta with a B:C ratio of 4.57. In Bihar, integration of raised beds, drip fertigation and poly-mulching improved nutrient-use efficiency by 30–85%. Adoption of drip irrigation and protected cultivation reduced irrigation water requirement by 70–80%, while hydroponics reduced water use by up to 90%. Drone-based foliar nutrient application improved crop yields by 4–5%, reduced spraying costs by about 15%, enabled spraying of one acre in about 6 minutes using only 9.5 litres of water and 0.5 litre of nano-fertilizer, while minimizing crop damage and ensuring uniform application. These technologies collectively enhance farm income, optimize water and fertilizer use, reduce production costs and support sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural growth.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

The integration of AI, IoT, drones, and satellite imagery enhances livestock management by creating proactive early disease warning systems, strengthening biosecurity, and optimizing overall farm efficiency include:

Predictive Disease Control and Reduced Mortality: AI models and IoT-enabled biometric sensors can detect physiological stress and predict potential disease outbreaks 5–12 days before clinical symptoms appear, enabling timely intervention. This can reduce veterinary expenses by 20–40% while preventing large-scale livestock losses.

Optimized Productivity and Reproductive Performance: Real-time wearable sensors automate estrus detection, improving the success rate of artificial insemination by 15–30%. In addition, smart microclimate control and precision feed management can enhance milk yields by up to 18%, leading to improved overall livestock productivity.

This information was given by Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297739.title: CULTIVATION OF KALA NAMAK RICE
2297739.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
CULTIVATION OF KALA NAMAK RICE
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

The area under cultivation and productivity of Kalanamak rice has increased in the recent past augmenting the farmers’ income. Production in Siddharthnagar district of Uttar Pradesh has increased to more than five times during 2018 to 2025. The sale price of Kalanamak rice has also increased from Rs 40/kg in 2018 to Rs. 150/kg in 2026 resulting into more than three fold increase in profitability vis-a-vis normal rice and boosting the number of farmers cultivating Kalanamak paddy from 2915 in 2018 to 23000 in 2024.

Both the Central Government and State Governments have provided financial, technical and marketing support to Kalanamak rice farmers. Under the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) and One District One Product (ODOP) Margin Money Scheme (state funded), individual micro-units and FPOs setting up Kalanamak processing/ milling units receive credit-linked capital subsidies up to 35% (max ₹10 lakh). The Government is also promoting brand Kalanamak by organising Kalanamak Mahotsavs. A Common Facility Centre (CFC) for Kalanamak rice in Siddharthnagar has been established under One District One Product (ODOP) scheme to provide local farmers with modern processing, packaging, and export-support facilities. The State Government has earmarked dedicated project funding for the promotion, production, and processing of Kalanamak rice.

National Agricultural Research System under the aegis of ICAR is involved in development of varieties and conservation of large number of land races of Kalanamak rice.  In addition to traditional Kalanamak varieties, six improved varieties viz. Kalanamak KN3. Bauna  Kalanamak  101, Bauna  Kalanamak  102, Kalanamak Kiran, Pusa Narendra Kalanamak 1 and Pusa CRD Kalanamak 2 have been released and notified. The later two dwarf high yielding varieties of Kalanamak have average yield of 4.5 tons/ha against 2.5 tons/ha of traditional varieties. State Government has also notified the KVKs in Geographical Indication (GI) area of Kalanamak for muti-location testing of new high yielding, climate resilient varieties for their release. ICAR-Institutes/ Krishi Vigyan Kendras are facilitating the farmers in registration and conservation of traditional Kalanamak rice varieties with the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Rights Authority, which has led to registration of more than 1700 land races and local varieties of rice.

For further increase in the area of Kalanamak rice, additional seed indents are also encouraged under Breeder Seed Program and around 15-20 quintals Breeder seed is produced every year for downstream multiplication of foundation and certified seeds by the indenting agencies. During last 5 years (2021-22 to 2025-26), a total of 389.6 quintals of quality seed of Kalanamak paddy varieties has been produced and distributed to farmers.

The Government promotes export of Kalanamak rice and facilitating access to international markets through Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) linking regional Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) directly to international buyers, facilitating export shipments to markets like Singapore and Nepal. Branding of Kalanamak rice as "Buddha Rice" promotes its cultural legacy to target high-value markets in Buddhist nations such as Japan, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, and Myanmar. Siddharthnagar and its surrounding Terai districts have been integrated into APEDA's Agri-Export Zone framework for specialty rice, facilitating priority financial assistance for export packaging, residue testing, and quarantine compliance.

This information was given by Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297740.title: Storage Capacity in PACS
2297740.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
Storage Capacity in PACS
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector 12  PACS/Cooperative Societies with a capacity of 0.52 LMT have been identified in 12 districts of the state and detailed project report in respect of all 13 projects have been prepared. However, construction is yet to be started by the States. Further, one godown of 1,500 MT capacity has already been constructed in Kotwa Pandey PACS in Mirzapur district of Uttar Pradesh. The Plan is demand-driven and implementation is undertaken in phased manner on the proposals received from State /UTs and therefore no state wise target is fixed. However, as per the AMI guidelines of DA&FW, construction of godowns by PACS/Cooperative Societies to be completed within 18 months and to submit completion documents for final subsidy claims. However, an extension of up to 6 additional months can be allowed if the reasons for delay are fully justified.

Under the Plan, financial assistance is available only for construction of new scientific storage infrastructure at PACS/other cooperative society level. All the godowns under decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector are created after the launch of the plan. Old or dilapidated PACS buildings are not treated as modern scientific warehouses under the plan.

To enable faster sanction of loan, a series of measures were undertaken under the plan. Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), the loan repayment period has been enhanced from 2+5 years to 2+8 years, thereby providing greater flexibility to borrowers.  Nabhsanrakshan scheme credit guarantee was also extended to PACS at par with Farmer Producer Organization (FPO). Under the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) Scheme, the capital subsidy has been enhanced from 25% to 33.33%, the margin money requirement has been reduced from 20% to 10%. Besides this the Plan also utilizes NABARD's special refinance scheme to significantly reduce the financial burden on participating cooperatives. When combined with the 3% interest subvention available under the AIF, the effective loan interest rate for PACS is reduced to 1% under Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector.

Further, under decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector eligible cooperative societies, including PACS, may establish infrastructure on either self-owned land or leased land. Land allocation is facilitated by the concerned State Governments, wherever required. Issues relating to land availability, loan sanction and financial capacity of PACS/other cooperative societies are addressed in coordination with the State Governments and the implementing agencies.

There is no such provision for separate quota or special subsidy for storage charges under the decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

2297736.title: Financial Irregularities in Cooperative Societies
2297736.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
Financial Irregularities in Cooperative Societies
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi

As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), out of a total 8.53 lakh Cooperative Societies across the country, 6.63 lakh are functional, 1.41 lakh are non-functional and 49,177 are under liquidation. Among 6.63 lakh functional cooperative societies, 5.95 lakh societies are audited and 0.68 lakh societies are not audited. The State-wise details of functional and audited cooperatives societies are attached as Annexure-1. The details of cooperative societies lying dormant due to financial irregularities, weak management and lack of timely audits is maintained by respective State / UTs.

Further, Cooperative Societies registered under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 function as autonomous cooperative organisations and accountable to their members. In case of irregularities including financial embezzlement, winding up proceeding u/s 86 of the MSCS Act, 2002 are initiated against such MSCSs and liquidator is appointed under the provisions of Section 89 of MSCS Act, 2002 to liquidate the assets of Society and to ensure payment to investors/members under the provisions of section 90 of the Act. So far, 115 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are put under liquidation. The State-wise number of such societies is attached as Annexure-2.

  1. The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several initiatives to ensure transparency, accountability and protection of members' interests in cooperative societies under the vision of "Sahakar-se-Samriddhi."  Key initiatives include:
  • The Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 was amended in 2023 to strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and reform electoral process, etc. in the Multi State Cooperative Societies (MSCS).
  • A Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund was established under section 63A of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act, 2023 to revive sick Multi-State Cooperative Societies and provide financial assistance for meeting their infrastructure requirements.
  • Circulation of Model Byelaws of PACS, enabling diversification of activities such as storage, processing, LPG distribution, and common service centers, ensuring better governance standards and promoting member-centric operations.
  • Strengthening of PACS through Computerization of PACS project by bringing functional PACS onto a common ERP-based national software, thereby improving transparency, efficiency, record management and service delivery.
  • Capacity building and skill development programmes through National Council for Co-operative Training (NCCT) for members, Board of Directors, employees of cooperative, state officials and aspiring youth across the country with a network of 20 training institutes.
  • Development of the National Cooperative Database (NCD) which serves as a comprehensive digital repository of 8.53 lakh cooperative societies across the country, having approximately 32 crore members.
  • Inclusion of Rural Cooperative Banks under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme to bring greater transparency and accountability.
