2297098.title: HEIs Progress in NIRF Ranking
2297098.body_html:
Ministry of Education
HEIs Progress in NIRF Ranking
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, lays emphasis on improving the overall quality of education in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) through a set of initiatives that include promotion of multidisciplinary education, nurturing critical thinking and analytical ability, promoting research and innovation, improving the quality of infrastructure, effective and qualitative teacher training etc.

The National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) was launched in 2015 by the Government of India for the annual ranking of institutions/universities of higher education in India (called India Rankings), to promote a healthy competition among educational institutes and universities. The methodology of these rankings is based on five broad parameters which are “Teaching, Learning and Resources,” “Research and Professional Practices,” “Graduation Outcomes,” “Outreach and Inclusivity,” and “Peer Perception”. The number of applications received under NIRF increased from 6,272 in 2021 to 14,163 in 2025. The number of unique institutions participating in NIRF increased from 4,030 to 7,692 during 2021-2025.

Since the launch of NIRF, there has been an increase in the number of institutions appearing in the QS World University Rankings. It has increased from 11 institutions in QS WUR 2015 to 52 in QS WUR 2027.

To improve Quality of Education, several initiatives have been institutionalised in Centrally Funded Institutions. Government of India also provides financial support to State Governments under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)/ Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM USHA) scheme under three components namely, “Enhancing Quality and Excellence in select State Universities”, “Infrastructure Grants to Universities” and “MultiDisciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU)” for improvement in Higher Education.

Further, World Class Institutions Scheme, also known as Institutions of Eminence (IoE) Scheme was launched in 2017 to create distinct category of institutions with great deal of autonomy in academic, administrative and financial matters so as to enable them to emerge as World Class Academic and Research Institutions in a reasonable time period.

The Government of India has established 43 new premier institutes since 2014 which include seven IIT’s, eight Central universities and 9 IIM’s. Most recently, IIM Guwahati was inaugurated in February 2026 as the 22nd IIM. The institute is currently operating from its transit campus in Kamrup district, Assam. To support its development, the government has allocated Rs 555 crores for setting up the temporary campus, initiating construction of the permanent facility, and ensuring smooth operations during its first five years.

Further, the Government of India has approved expansion of academic and infrastructure capacity including creation of Research Park of five new IITs which had been established in the State/UT of Andhra Pradesh (IIT Tirupati), Kerala (IIT Palakkad), Chhattisgarh (IIT Bhilai), Jammu & Kashmir (IIT Jammu) and Karnataka (IIT Dharwad) with a total outlay of Rs. 11,828.79 crore in May, 2025.

To promote skill-integrated education with industry requirements in schools and colleges, several initiatives have been undertaken by Ministry of Education including: 

  • To upgrade school curricula, the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), in collaboration with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), has developed resources for computational thinking and AI Curriculum for both teachers and students from grade 3 to 8. 
  • To develop the capacity of teachers in leveraging technology, focused efforts have been made by NCERT in organising training activities on AI, covering more than 96,000 beneficiaries through these programs. Similarly, CBSE organises capacity building programmes to sensitise teachers to the application of AI tools in teaching, learning, and assessment, as well as their relevance in educational management and administration. In the last 3 years, 1,234 programmes have been conducted, benefitting 64,775 teachers of CBSE affiliated schools.
  • UGC has also introduced “Guidelines for Internship/Research Internship for Under Graduate Students”, to improve employability, develop interest for research and provide exposure to emerging technologies.
  • Further, UGC has formulated the “Guidelines for Higher Educational Institutions to Offer Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP)” to embed the competencies required by the industry in the university curriculum. 
  • To enhance employability of the students, the National Credit Framework (NCrF) has been issued by UGC, enabling integration of skill education into academia, having a provision for the accumulation of a maximum of 50% of the total credit required through skill-based courses.
  • AICTE periodically revises its Model Curriculum in consultation with academia, industry, professional bodies, and Institutions of National Importance to ensure alignment with industry requirements and technological advancements like Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science (DS), Machine Learning (ML), Cyber Security, Robotics, Quantum Computing, and other emerging technologies across technical disciplines. 
  • AICTE is actively strengthening skill development by embedding it into technical education. It partners with industries and institutions to offer online skill courses aligned with the regular curriculum, along with skill-focused programmes, compulsory internships, and vocational degrees. 
  • AICTE has made Internships an integral component of technical education to provide students with practical industry exposure and enhance employability. 
  • The Ministry of Education implements the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) to impart on-the-job training in collaboration with industry to enhance the employability of youth.
  • Further, to strengthen industry-academia linkages and enhance learners' employability, the Ministry of Education in collaboration with eminent industry partners, has launched the SWAYAM Plus platform. The platform offers more than 500 employability-focused courses across 15 sectors in collaboration with 89 industries.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

2297094.title: Alignment of NCERT Syllabus with National Education Policy 2020
2297094.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Alignment of NCERT Syllabus with National Education Policy 2020 
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

As per the recommendations of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the National  Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has brought out the National Curriculum  Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) 2022 and the National Curriculum Framework for  School Education (NCF-SE) 2023. These frameworks provide the basis for stage-wise and subject wise curricular goals, competencies, learning outcomes, syllabi, textbooks, pedagogy and  assessment. 

For developing National Curriculum Frameworks, National Steering Committee was constituted  which followed bottom -up approach of seeking inputs for the National Curriculum Frameworks  from diverse stakeholders including teachers, parents, students, educational institutions, neo- and  non- literates, subjects’ experts, scholars, Anganwadi personnel etc., from across the states and UTs,  a massive process of public consultations in face-to-face as well as digital mode was conducted.  This process had benefited from the engagement of over 13 lakh interested citizens including  students and parents at the national level through citizen-centric mobile app survey and over 1.5  lakh teachers, parents, students, and educationists at the state level through mobile app survey. 

Over 1550 district-level consultations in 32 States and Union Territories were conducted. Inputs  were also received from 35 groups of institutions, 8000 stakeholders who attended 12 consultations  with Universities and Civil Society Groups. More than 600 position papers on 25 specifically  relevant themes written by Focus Groups constituted by the States and UTs which all together had  over 4000 experts, and 25 papers from the National Focus Groups by expert groups with over 175  members, constituted by the NCERT. These inputs were analyzed and relevant suggestions were  included in the NCFs. Taking cognizance of these inputs, the NCF-FS was released on 20th October,  2022 and NCF-SE was released on 23rd August, 2023. 

As a follow-up of the NCFs, NCERT has constituted National Syllabus and Teaching-Learning  Material Committee (NSTC). Under this Committee, 13 Curricular Area Groups (CAGs) and  Textbook Development Teams (TDTs) for all the subjects and grades have been set up. NSTC has  been assigned the task of development of teaching-learning material including textbooks. NCERT  has also constituted National Curriculum Framework Oversight Committee (NOC) to look into the  translation of NCF perspective in the new teaching-learning material including textbooks. NSTC,  NOC and CAG include scholars, subject experts, renowned players, artists, teacher educators,  faculty members of NCERT, officials from SCERTs, etc. TDT includes scholars, subject experts,  teachers, teacher educators, faculty members of NCERT, faculty members from SCERTs, etc. With  the support of NSTC, NCERT has brought out new syllabus and textbooks for Grades 1-9 and also  a collection of learning resources- Jaadui Pitara and e Jaadui Pitara for Balvatika 1, 2, and 3. 

New teaching-learning material including textbooks and learning material are developed through  detailed mapping of curricular goals, competencies and learning outcomes. The drafts undergo  multiple rounds of academic, pedagogical, language and sensitivity review. The review process  examines academic accuracy, age-appropriateness, inclusivity, constitutional values, gender  sensitivity, cultural and linguistic relevance, pedagogical suitability and alignment with NEP 2020,  NCF-FS 2022 and NCF-SE 2023. As a follow-up of the NCF-SE, Learning Outcome Document and  Mandate Documents were developed, which served as guidelines for the development of new syllabi  and textbooks along with NCF-FS and NCF-SE. 

NCERT, while reprinting its textbooks, every year, updates its textbooks in alignment with the  relevant feedback from students, teachers and other stakeholders, without making any structural  changes. For this purpose, also, if required, NCERT invites experts for finalizing the changes. 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297090.title: Implementation and Impact of the National Credit Framework (NCrF)
2297090.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Implementation and Impact of the National Credit Framework (NCrF) 
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with  an aim to provide holistic, multidisciplinary, flexible and student-centric education. It  encourages integration of skill education & envisions a detailed National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) as the basis for Recognition of Prior Learning.

In alignment with the objectives of NEP 2020, the Government has approved the National Credit Framework (NCrF) as a comprehensive credit framework encompassing elementary, school,  higher, and skill education. The NCrF provides for creditisation of all learning and assignment,  accumulation, storage, transfer & redemption of credits, subject to assessment; and establishes  academic equivalence among skill, general and experiential education while enabling  mobility within & between them. As reported in AISHE 2023-24, more than 700 Universities and over 7,500 affiliated colleges have adopted NCrF. 

The University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified “SOP for Operationalisation of National Credit Framework in Higher Education” as a practical guide for implementation of  NCrF. The SOP allows up to 50% of the total credits for a program to be earned from the skill based courses. 

The All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) in its Approval Process Handbook (APH) 2023-27, sets norms for Entry Level Qualifications for the Technical Programmes in accordance with NCrF. It allows 10th + 2-year ITIs students to be eligible for admission to Second Year Diploma course(s) in any branch of Engineering and Technology. Further, lateral  entry to Third Year is available for candidates possessing a 2-year UG Diploma in Engineering (NCrF Level 5.0). 

Further, the National Council of Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has developed  “Guidelines for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)”. The guidelines delineate a roadmap for  the seamless implementation of RPL, and empower the industrial bodies to conduct RPL assessments for their workforces. This aligns the assessment process in a manner that meets  the industry's needs. Credits are awarded based on assessment of learning outcomes of the specific skills, competencies and knowledge acquired. 

Due to concerted efforts by the Government, India’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education increased from 23.7 in 2014–15 to 30 in 2023–24. Female GER rose from 22.9 to 31.2 during the same period. The rise in GER has been accompanied by significant growth in student enrolment, with total higher education enrolment increasing from 3.42 crore in 2014-15 to 4.50 crore in 2023–24, adding more than 1.08 crore students to the higher education system. 

NEP 2020 envisions an education system rooted in Indian ethos that contributes directly to transforming India, into an equitable and vibrant knowledge society, by providing high-quality education to all. NCrF aims to contribute to this vision by establishing equivalence and mobility between general and skill education so that lifelong learning, recognition of prior learning, multiple entry and exit, and continuous professional development is encouraged in the  education ecosystem. 

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

2297088.title: Response of Teachers to Reappear for TET
2297088.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Response of Teachers to Reappear for TET 
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi

Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the recruitment, service  conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the respective State  Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 

The Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated 01.09.2025, inter alia, held that the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the minimum qualifications prescribed under Section 23 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and is mandatory for appointment as a teacher in schools covered under the Act. The Supreme Court further directed that eligible  teachers shall acquire the prescribed TET qualification within the timeline specified in the judgment.  The order of the Supreme Court may be accessed at the following link: 

https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63764_Judgement_01-Sep 2025.pdf 

Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide judgment dated 29.05.2026, the Supreme Court extended the timeline for acquisition of TET qualification from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028. The Supreme Court further observed that the respective appropriate Governments/authorities should endeavour to conduct the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) periodically,  preferably twice every year, with an interval of approximately six months between successive  examinations, so as to afford eligible teachers a reasonable opportunity to comply with the prescribed minimum qualification. The judgment dated 29.05.2026 may be accessed at the following link: 

https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_Judgement_29-May 2026.pdf

The Supreme Court, while taking into consideration the practical difficulties faced by in-service teachers recruited prior to the enactment of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, invoked its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and directed that such teachers who have less than five years of service remaining, as on the date of the judgment dated  01.09.2025, may continue in service till attaining the age of superannuation without acquiring the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) qualification. The Supreme Court further clarified that such teachers shall  not be eligible for promotion unless they acquire the prescribed TET qualification. 

This information was given by Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

State-wise detail of funds allocated for elementary education under Samagra Shiksha during the last three years and the current year is at Annexure.

Financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha. Accordingly, annual plans under Samagra Shiksha are prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority and this is reflected in their respective Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B). These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme. The funds are released based on the fulfilment of certain conditions such as pace of expenditure, receipt of commensurate State share, audited accounts, statement cumulative State share, statement on outstanding advances, up-to date expenditure statement, furnishing of information as prescribed in the Manual on Financial Management & Procurement and audited utilization certificate of previous year. The unspent balances of last year are taken into account while releasing the funds. Some of the States are not able to receive all instalments owing to the slow pace of their expenditure.

This Department has launched the PRABANDH (Project Appraisal, Budgeting Achievements and Data Handling) System. One of the important features of the PRABANDH System is updation of Expenditure incurred under the different interventions of the Samagra Shiksha. For this purpose, a data visualization Dashboard has been created in the PRABANDH System for display of monthly status of physical and financial progress under the major interventions of the Samagra Shiksha. Regular follow ups and review meetings are held with the States/UTs ensuring an integrated approach for monitoring and smooth implementation of the schemes.

2297085.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with Commonwealth Games champions
2297085.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with Commonwealth Games champions
PM highlights national sports success relies on building a comprehensive sports culture, beyond just physical infrastructure
PM emphasises medals inspire young students in schools far more than any verbal encouragement
PM congratulates athletes for bringing glory to the nation and expresses confidence in their future victories
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi

Prime minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with India’s Commonwealth Games Champions. The Prime Minister observed the transforming landscape of Indian sports over the past decade, highlighting that receiving national sportspersons at his residence has been a regular and cherished tradition throughout his 12 to 13-year tenure. He affirmed that the dedicated efforts and sustained successes of Indian athletes in securing continuous victories for the country inspire young school students far more effectively than routine promotional advice. “Your medal inspires them more than anything we could say by going to schools,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister interacted with an athlete who recalled a prior commitment regarding her daughters taking up sports, following up on her progress and receiving an assurance that her daughters would bring home three medals in the upcoming Commonwealth Games. He warmly validated her confidence and encouraged her commitment to excellence.

The Prime Minister recognized the deep emotional journey of the athletes, remarking on the perseverance of a player who dedicated a victory achieved on Guru Purnima to his coach, and another athlete who broke into tears on the podium after overcoming four years of persistent injuries and personal hardships to see the National Flag raised. He noted that such national triumphs transcend individual achievements to become an enduring source of inspiration for future generations. “This victory of yours becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations,” affirmed Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister discussed the growing respect and fear commanded by Indian athletes on the international circuit, noting that global competitors now feel intimidated when drawn against Indian opponents. He specifically highlighted the rising stature of Indian boxers and acknowledged the feedback from athletes regarding the transformative role played by grassroots initiatives like the Khelo India Scheme and back-to-back competition support provided by the government. “World players have now started fearing these boxers too,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister emphasized the core philosophy behind sports promotion, stating that athletes must continue to maintain the humble spirit of a young learner while expanding the prestige of the Khelo India initiative. He added that true national sports success depends not merely on physical infrastructure, but on building a comprehensive sports culture across the nation. “Sports infrastructure is one thing, but the country achieves medals when a sports culture is built in the country,” stated Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister acknowledged the patriotism of an Indian Army athlete who defeated his Pakistani opponent 5-0 on Kargil Vijay Diwas and dedicated his victory to the heroes of the Indian Army, remarking that such deep national pride adds extraordinary luster to athletic triumphs. He also shared lighthearted moments with an athlete recounting a humorous anecdote about his army coach, Narendra Rana, and the shared name "Narendra." “You have not merely increased the number of medals; you have prepared a generation,” noted Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister praised an athlete who expressed gratitude to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) for providing crucial training facilities to them, which enabled a transition from local sports centers to international podium finishes. “It is a matter of great honor for me; you did the hard work and remembered me, and I am very grateful to you,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister made inquiries regarding the upgraded sports infrastructure across various regional hubs, including Varanasi and Bhopal, where athletes spent time training and visiting spiritual sites like Kashi Vishwanath and Mahakaleshwar in Ujjain. He commended the continuous support provided by the SAI and the Khelo India framework since its inception in 2018, which has helped young talent transition smoothly to elite competitive levels. “Rest assured, in the future too you will be victorious and once again we will meet right here,” stated Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister extended his warm wishes and blessings to a multi-time medalist who celebrated her birthday during the interaction, personally offering sweets to mark the occasion and encouraging all athletes to maintain their winning momentum with a positive outlook. He smiled and gave his blessings to the contingent for their continuous third consecutive medal-winning streak. “He who plays, blooms”, asserted Shri Modi.

2297053.title: DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN THE NORTH-EASTERN REGION
2297053.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN THE NORTH-EASTERN REGION
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Tourism as part of its ongoing endeavour, promotes various tourism destinations and products of India including the states of North Eastern region in a holistic manner, through various initiatives including promotional events, assistance to State Governments/UT Administrations for organising fairs and festivals, participation in exhibitions, websites, social media etc.

The Ministry of Tourism has been organizing International Tourism Mart (ITM) in the North Eastern Region since 2013. The ITM is an annual event designed to highlight the tourism potential of the North Eastern region for both domestic and international audiences. This event serves as a vital platform, bringing together tourism businesses and entrepreneurs from the eight North Eastern States—Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim—to foster collaboration and interactions among buyers, sellers, media, government agencies, and other stakeholders. The latest   ITM was held at Gangtok, Sikkim, from 13-16 November 2025. In addition to this the followings steps including the initiatives under various central schemes as under:

(i) Incredible India Digital Platform-The Ministry of Tourism revamped the Incredible India website as IIDP in September 2024 to engage the visitors across web and social media platforms. The content on the Incredible India Website is available in Hindi, English and UN languages. The website features tourism destination in the North East States to promote tourism in NER.

(ii)The Ministry of Tourism promotes various tourism sites and products in North East Region in the domestic and international markets. Creative posts, Live sessions, Tweets etc., on North East destinations are posted on regular basis on the social media handles of the Ministry of Tourism. In addition, the Ministry of Tourism also produces promotional material showcasing the tourist destinations and products in North Eastern States.

(iii)Central Financial Assistance (CFA) support for organizing fairs & festivals- Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance to State Governments/UT Administrations for organising fairs / festivals and Tourism related events under the DPPH scheme. The list of North East States to which the financial support for organizing fairs and festivals has been extended is at Annexure-II.

(iv) Ministry of Tourism under the schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan’, ‘National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’, ‘Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development’ provides financial assistance to State Governments/Union Territory Administrations/Central Agencies, Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI Scheme), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD) for the development of tourism related infrastructure and facilities at various tourism destinations in the country including North Eastern Region. The Ministry of Tourism has now revamped the Swadesh Darshan Scheme as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD 2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and responsible tourism destinations, following a destination & tourism centric approach. The details of projects sanctioned under the above-mentioned schemes in North Eastern region are given at Annexure-III.

Ministry of Tourism implements the Swachhta Action Plan (SAP) in coordination with the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti. Under SAP, the Ministry conducts cleanliness-awareness programmes, including in the North Eastern States. During 2025–26, 200 SAP activities were organized through IITTM, Central IHMs, State IHMs and FCIs under the following categories of (i) Tourist Awareness (ii) Students Awareness (iii) Stakeholders Awareness. Additionally, as directed by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the Ministry of Tourism observes Swachhta Pakhwada and Swachhta Hi Sewa (SHS) every year in September and October. In 2025, 277 activities under Swachhta Pakhwada and 244 activities under SHS were carried out across India, including the North Eastern Region.

For effective air connectivity at PAN Indian basis including the States of NER, the Ministry of Civil Aviation launched the RCS-UDAN scheme to make regional air travel affordable, and the Ministry of Tourism has collaborated with it by extending Viability Gap Funding under the Champion Service Sector Scheme to improve air links to key tourist locations, including in the North Eastern Region. Under this initiative, the following NER routes have been included as Tourism RCS routes: Dibrugarh–Dimapur, Dimapur–Dibrugarh, Dimapur–Imphal, Imphal–Dimapur, Agartala–Aizawl, Aizawl–Agartala, Dibrugarh–Imphal, Imphal–Dibrugarh, Hollongi–Guwahati and Guwahati–Hollongi.

This information was given by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a reply in the Lok Sabha today.

2297031.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with India’s Commonwealth Games champions
2297031.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with India’s Commonwealth Games champions
Your medal inspires youngsters more than anything we could say by going to schools: PM
Your victory is a big inspiration for the coming generations: PM
Nation wins medals when a sports culture is built in the country: PM
He who plays, blooms: PM
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi

Prime minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with India’s Commonwealth Games Champions. The Prime Minister observed the transforming landscape of Indian sports over the past decade, highlighting that receiving national sportspersons at his residence has been a regular and cherished tradition throughout his 12 to 13-year tenure. He affirmed that the dedicated efforts and sustained successes of Indian athletes in securing continuous victories for the country inspire young school students far more effectively than routine promotional advice. “Your medal inspires them more than anything we could say by going to schools,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister interacted with an athlete who recalled a prior commitment regarding her daughters taking up sports, following up on her progress and receiving an assurance that her daughters would bring home three medals in the upcoming Commonwealth Games. He warmly validated her confidence and encouraged her commitment to excellence.

The Prime Minister recognized the deep emotional journey of the athletes, remarking on the perseverance of a player who dedicated a victory achieved on Guru Purnima to his coach, and another athlete who broke into tears on the podium after overcoming four years of persistent injuries and personal hardships to see the National Flag raised. He noted that such national triumphs transcend individual achievements to become an enduring source of inspiration for future generations. “This victory of yours becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations,” affirmed Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister discussed the growing respect and fear commanded by Indian athletes on the international circuit, noting that global competitors now feel intimidated when drawn against Indian opponents. He specifically highlighted the rising stature of Indian boxers and acknowledged the feedback from athletes regarding the transformative role played by grassroots initiatives like the Khelo India Scheme and back-to-back competition support provided by the government. “World players have now started fearing these boxers too,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister emphasized the core philosophy behind sports promotion, stating that athletes must continue to maintain the humble spirit of a young learner while expanding the prestige of the Khelo India initiative. He added that true national sports success depends not merely on physical infrastructure, but on building a comprehensive sports culture across the nation. “Sports infrastructure is one thing, but the country achieves medals when a sports culture is built in the country,” stated Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister acknowledged the patriotism of an Indian Army athlete who defeated his Pakistani opponent 5-0 on Kargil Vijay Diwas and dedicated his victory to the heroes of the Indian Army, remarking that such deep national pride adds extraordinary luster to athletic triumphs. He also shared lighthearted moments with an athlete recounting a humorous anecdote about his army coach, Narendra Rana, and the shared name "Narendra." “You have not merely increased the number of medals; you have prepared a generation,” noted Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister praised an athlete who expressed gratitude to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) for providing crucial training facilities to them, which enabled a transition from local sports centers to international podium finishes. “It is a matter of great honor for me; you did the hard work and remembered me, and I am very grateful to you,” remarked Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister made inquiries regarding the upgraded sports infrastructure across various regional hubs, including Varanasi and Bhopal, where athletes spent time training and visiting spiritual sites like Kashi Vishwanath and Mahakaleshwar in Ujjain. He commended the continuous support provided by the SAI and the Khelo India framework since its inception in 2018, which has helped young talent transition smoothly to elite competitive levels. “Rest assured, in the future too you will be victorious and once again we will meet right here,” stated Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister extended his warm wishes and blessings to a multi-time medalist who celebrated her birthday during the interaction, personally offering sweets to mark the occasion and encouraging all athletes to maintain their winning momentum with a positive outlook. He smiled and gave his blessings to the contingent for their continuous third consecutive medal-winning streak. “He who plays, blooms ”, asserted Shri Modi.

2297026.title: Welfare Schemes for Hill-Based Minority Communities implemented by  Ministry of Minority Affairs
2297026.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Welfare Schemes for Hill-Based Minority Communities implemented by  Ministry of Minority Affairs
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Minority Affairs implements the following schemes/programmes for socio-economic empowerment of the six (6) centrally notified minority communities namely Buddhists, Christians, Jains, Muslims, Parsis and Sikhs across the country including the state of West Bengal irrespective of any topographic conditions:

1. PRADHAN MANTRI VIRASAT KA SAMVARDHAN (PM VIKAS)

The Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), an integrated Central Sector Scheme by combining the five erstwhile livelihood schemes, namely Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil, to facilitate opportunities for minority communities in education, skilling and employment. The Scheme comprises four components, namely (i) Skilling and Training, (ii) Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship, (iii) Education, and (iv) Infrastructure Development through convergence with Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), wherever required.

2. PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM (PMJVK)

PMJVK, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aims to create community infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas across the country in sectors such as Health, Education, Skill Development, Women-centric Projects, Drinking Water and Sanitation, Sports, Renewable Energy and other community infrastructure.

3. CONCESSIONAL CREDIT SCHEMES OF NATIONAL MINORITIES DEVELOPMENT & FINANCE CORPORATION (NMDFC)

So far as NMDFC is concerned, it is functioning to promote the socio-economic development of the notified minority communities, namely Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains, across the country, including hill-based minority communities.

Under Credit Line-1 (CL-1), persons having an annual family income of up to ₹3.00 lakh are eligible for financial assistance under NMDFC schemes. Under Credit Line-2 (CL-2), persons having an annual family income of up to ₹8.00 lakh are eligible for financial assistance.

NMDFC implements its concessional credit schemes through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) nominated by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. In the State of West Bengal, the West Bengal Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (WBMDFC) is the designated State Channelising Agency and implements NMDFC schemes for eligible minority beneficiaries, including those belonging to hill-based minority communities, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines.

This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

2297024.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Special Leadership and Capacity-Building Programmes by Ministry of Minority Affairs for minority women in Odisha
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi

Under the erstwhile schemes of the Ministry of Minority Affairs, the Ministry implemented the Leadership Development of Minority Women (Nai Roshni) scheme to empower and build their confidence among minority women by providing knowledge, tools and techniques for interacting with Government systems, banks and other institutions at all levels. The scheme aimed to enhance leadership qualities, promote awareness about rights and entitlements, and facilitate socio-economic empowerment of minority women. The scheme was implemented across the country, including the State of Odisha, through empanelled Project Implementing Agencies.

Further, the Ministry has now subsumed various welfare schemes under the integrated umbrella scheme PM VIKAS (Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan). PM VIKAS focuses on the socio-economic and educational empowerment of six notified minority communities through skill development, Leadership & entrepreneurship development, education support and infrastructure-related interventions.

Minority women, including from the state of Odisha, are eligible to participate in and benefit from the various components of PM VIKAS, including skill development, Leadership Development & Entrepreneurship and related capacity-building initiatives, subject to the scheme guidelines.

This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

2297013.title: DGFT Removes Physical Duty Payment Challans for Export Obligation Discharge Certificate Applications under Advance Authorisation and Export Promotion Capital Goods Schemes
2297013.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DGFT Removes Physical Duty Payment Challans for Export Obligation Discharge Certificate Applications under Advance Authorisation and Export Promotion Capital Goods Schemes
Physical Challans Dispensed with for Voluntary Duty Payments from 1 August 2026
DGFT–ICEGATE API Integration Enables Direct Access to Authenticated Customs Duty Payment Records
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 1:29PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant Ease of Doing Business measure for exporters, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has removed the requirement of submitting physical duty payment challans while applying for Export Obligation Discharge Certificates (EODC) under the Advance Authorisation (AA) and Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Schemes. Licence-wise voluntary duty payment data received from Customs/ICEGATE has been integrated with DGFT’s online systems, enabling authenticated verification of such payments directly against the concerned authorisation.

For voluntary duty payments made on or after 1 August 2026, exporters will no longer be required to submit physical challans along with their applications for closure of authorisations. Authenticated payment details will be made available to exporters on the DGFT Customer Portal, enabling them to verify that the payment has been correctly mapped to the concerned authorisation before filing the application.

The same authenticated payment record will be available to the Regional Authorities on the DGFT Back Office, eliminating the need for manual verification of payment particulars. This is expected to facilitate faster processing, reduce avoidable correspondence and bring greater consistency in decision-making across DGFT Regional Authorities.

The digital facility has been implemented through an API-based data exchange between DGFT and ICEGATE, under which duty payment particulars are transmitted electronically from Customs systems to DGFT’s EODC processing workflow. The replacement of manual submission and verification with authenticated digital records is expected to shorten processing timelines, improve data accuracy, minimise human intervention and enhance transparency in the closure process.

The measure is also expected to reduce transaction costs and compliance burden for exporters by reducing documentation, follow-up and physical interface, particularly benefiting MSME exporters handling closure formalities in-house. Trade Notice No. 15/2026-27 dated 5 August 2026 has been issued by DGFT for information of exporters and other stakeholders.

The initiative is part of the Government’s broader digital transformation agenda for trade facilitation, aimed at creating a more efficient, predictable and trust-based regulatory environment. By strengthening integration between trade-related digital systems and reducing reliance on physical documentation, the measure reinforces the vision of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” and enables exporters to focus on trade and growth.

The Advance Authorisation Scheme permits duty-free import of inputs that are physically incorporated in the export product, while the EPCG Scheme permits import of capital goods at concessional or zero customs duty, in both cases against an export obligation. Where the export obligation is not fulfilled in full, the authorisation holder regularises the case by voluntarily paying the proportionate customs duty saved along with applicable interest and thereafter applies for an EODC to close the authorisation. Earlier, proof of such payment was required to be submitted in physical form and verified manually by the Regional Authority.

2297002.title: Text of PM’s interaction with India's CWG champions
2297002.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM’s interaction with India's CWG champions
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 1:11PM by PIB Delhi

प्रधानमंत्री – मेरे यहां, मुझे यहां लगभग 12-13 साल हो गए इसी मकान में, अगर मैंने regularly और हर बार किसी को रिसिव किया है, किसी को मैं मिला हूं, तो खिलाड़ी हैं। पिछले 10-12 साल हो गए, आप लोगों के पुरुषार्थ के कारण, भारत को लगातार विजय दिलाने के आपके प्रयासों के कारण और उत्तरोत्तर सफलता में नई ऊंचाईयां पार करने की परंपरा के कारण, जो काम शायद हम स्कूलों में जाकर कहें कि नहीं नहीं भई खेलना चाहिए, ये करना चाहिए, वो काम स्कूलों में जाकर के हम कर सकते थे, उससे ज्यादा आपका मेडल उनको inspire करता है।

प्रधानमंत्री – तुमने मुझे वादा किया था पिछली बार कि तुम्हारी दोनों बेटियां खिलाड़ी बन जाएंगी?

खिलाड़ी - हाँ जी अभी वे उमर की छोटी हैं, अगले कॉमनवेल्थ में एक घर में तीन मेडल लाकर दिखाएंगी।

प्रधानमंत्री – पक्का।

खिलाड़ी – हाँ जी।

खिलाड़ी – जब मैं दौड़ रहा था, जब मेरा इवेंट था 29 को, तो उस दिन गुरुपूर्णिमा थी, तो उस दिन मेरे गुरू को मैंने एक गिफ्ट दे दिया।

प्रधानमंत्री – बड़ी शान बढ़ाई आपने। इतनी आंसू टपक रहे थे, मुझे लगता है कि आंसू के हर बूंद से जैसे गोल्ड मेडल टपक रहा है।

खिलाड़ी – मैं बहुत ज्यादा खुशी थी, इमोशनल भी थे उसी दिन, खुशी ज्यादा था और मैं इसलिए रोई थी कि मेरा पेरिस आलंपिक में मेरा 1 Kg में मेडल रह गई थी और एक प्लेयर्स की लाइफ में क्या क्या हमको फेस करना पड़ता है। तो ये 4 साल के अंदर में कितना क्या क्या कुछ मैंने फेस किया था, हर टाइम injury ही चल रहे थे और family problem, वो सब हो रहा था। तो बहुत मुश्किल से मैं ये 4 साल फेस किया था। तो वो सब जब पोडियम में जब मैं खड़ी थी सर और हमारी जो फ्लैग ऊपर जाते हैं और हमारे नेशनल एंथम जब बजते हैं तो सर हम रुक नहीं सकते सर, अपना आप आंसू निकलते हैं।

प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत बहुत बढ़िया

प्रधानमंत्री – आपके इस अचीवमेंट को सिर्फ आपका अचीवमेंट मानता हूं, ऐसा नहीं है, ये आपका विजय आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए बहुत बड़ी प्रेरणा बन जाता है।

खिलाड़ी – सब डर रहे थे हमसे कि इंडिया के साथ फाइट आ गई, अब तो हम पहली फाइट ही हार जायेंगे, हमारा मेडल भी नहीं आयेगा।

प्रधानमंत्री – यानी मान के चलते हैं।

खिलाड़ी – हाँ सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – क्या हुआ, वो restaurant वालों से झगड़ा कर रही थी?

खिलाड़ी – हम लोगों का जो इतना अच्छा परफॉर्मेंस था, लास्ट डे था और सब जीत के गए थे और पूरा इंडिया के लोग थे। तो थोड़ा सा मुझे बुरा लग रहा। तो मैंने उनको अच्छे से बोला रिक्वेस्ट किया था सर, फिर उन्होंने मान भी लिया, अभी चेंज भी हो गया सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – इस विजय की परिस्थिति खुशी, आनंद, अपने साथियों के साथ और गेम पूरे हो चुके हैं। तो हसी मजाक मस्ती का मूड ऐसे समय उस मैप पर नजर जाना और उसको रजिस्टर करना और तुरंत सिर्फ मेडल लेते समय देश खड़ा हो जाता है ऐसा नहीं, भीतर से देश का भाव मैं सच बताता हूँ ये वीडियो सामान्य नहीं है आपका, लंबे समय तक लोगों को याद रहेगा। ये बॉक्सिंग वालों से भी दुनिया के खिलाड़ी अब डरने लगे हैं।

खिलाड़ी – जरूर सर, पुरे सभी डरे हुए थे। एक के बाद एक गोल्ड मेडल गोल्ड मेडल आ रहे थे और मतलब पूरा लास्ट में ऐसे धमाका जैसा हो गया बिल्कुल। जिस तरीके से हम लोगों को सपोर्ट मिल रहा है, हमें बैक टू बैक कंपटीशन मिल रहा है वो एक बहुत बड़ी बात है और हमारे जितने भी यंग एथलीट है वो लोग सभी जैसे खेलो इंडिया स्कीम से आए हुए हैं और ये एक बहुत बड़ा changes ला रहा है पूरे स्पोर्ट्स में ही।

प्रधानमंत्री – अगर आप लोग खेलो इंडिया की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ाते हैं और प्रतिष्ठा सिर्फ वहां जाकर के रिबिन काटने से नहीं होगी। आप वैसे ही खेलेंगे जैसे एक छोटा विद्यार्थी, एक छोटा नौजवान, छोटा खिलाड़ी खेलता है। यह बहुत बड़ा कंट्रीब्यूशन करेगा। क्योंकि अभी तो हमें बहुत आगे जाना है, बहुत मेडल लाना है। कारगिल विजय दिवस पर किसकी विजय हुई थी?

खिलाड़ी – उस दिन कारगिल डे था वैसे और जिस दिन मैंने पाकिस्तान के साथ फाइट किया था सर, वो उसी दिन का था। तो मैं एक इंडियन आर्मी से हूं, तो मैंने उस दिन मैं पहले से बहुत वो था कि सर पाकिस्तान को हराना है। तो मैंने वो पाकिस्तान एक तरफ मैंने 5-0 से हराया, तो मैंने हमारा इंडियन आर्मी का कारगिल हीरोज़ को मैंने डेडिकेट किया किया था सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – आपको यह याद रहना और आप स्वयं फौज से हैं तो, मैं जरूर मानता हूं कि देश के वीर जवानों को आपने जो भाव प्रकट किया ना कि, मैं कारगिल के विजेताओं को मेरा मेडल समर्पित करता हूं। उसने उस विजय पर चार चांद लगा दिए और जिसको पराजित करना था उसी को किया आपने।

खिलाड़ी – वो पाकिस्तान की बात चल रही है, मुझे किस्सा याद आ गया सर। 2015 वर्ल्ड मिलिट्री गेम थे और मेरी पाकिस्तान के साथ पहली फाइट आ गई थी और वर्ल्ड मिलिट्री गेम थे तो मिलिट्री वाले के फोन आए कि भई पाकिस्तान से नहीं हारना है। तो फिर मैं फर्स्ट राउंड 4-1 से जीत गया। सेकंड राउंड 3-2 से जीत गया, पर दोनों के सर लग गए आपस में, तो दोनों के लग गए कट और फाइट तो मैं जीत गया।

प्रधानमंत्री – हाँ

खिलाड़ी – उसके बाद फिर दोनों चले गए हॉस्पिटल में टांके लगवाने के लिए। फिर 2014 में आप फर्स्ट टाइम प्रधानमंत्री जी बने थे और जो हमारे साथ आर्मी का कोच गया हुआ था उसका नाम नरेंद्र राणा था और फिर वो कई देर तक सोच के मेरे को बोला कि भाईजान एक बात बोलूं, मैं हां बोलो, बोला भाईजान आपका नाम नरेंद्र है। आपके कोच का नाम नरेंद्र है, आपके प्रधानमंत्री का नाम नरेंद्र है, तो मुझे नरेंद्र नाम से नफरत हो गई है।

प्रधानमंत्री – सिर्फ आपने मेडल की संख्या बढ़ाई ऐसा नहीं है। आपने एक पीढ़ी को तैयार किया।

खिलाड़ी – मेरे मन में भी धक-धक धक-धक हो रहा है सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – आप चिंता मत कीजिए।

खिलाड़ी – पर..

प्रधानमंत्री – आप चाहें तो आपको बोलने में भी मेडल मिलने वाला है।

खिलाड़ी – मेरे फ्रेंड सर्कल में किसी ने बोला था कि मैं उनको कुछ बोलती थी भई तुम्हारे अच्छे के लिए तुम करो। तो अक्सर मुझे वो बोलते थे कि तू के मोदी ते मिल रही है?

प्रधानमंत्री – हाँ

खिलाड़ी – हरियाणवी में बोल देते हैं सर कि क्या तू मोदी से मिली हुई है, कि तेरी बात माने। तो आज मैं आपसे मिली हूं सर। मैं उनको बोल पाऊंगी कि हां मैं मोदी जी से मिली हूं।

खिलाड़ी – कॉमनवेंल्थ गेम्स में मैंने सिल्वर मेडल जीता, फिर मैंने क्रेडिट साहब को दिया, सपना तो था एक बार मेडल जीत के लेके आने के लिए, बट ट्रेनिंग का सेंटर नहीं था, मैंने SAI आने के बाद मैं बहुत ट्रेनिंग करके मेडल जीत पा रहा, इसलिए बहुत खुशी से मैंने सर को क्रेडिट दिया था क्योंकि बहुत इंप्रूव हुआ।

प्रधानमंत्री – मेरे लिए बहुत बड़ा सम्मान का विषय है, मेहनत आपने की और मुझे याद किया, मैं आपका बहुत आभारी हूं दोस्त।

प्रधानमंत्री – वाराणसी में खेल तुम प्रैक्टिस कर रही थी ना?

खिलाड़ी – जी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – कैसा बना है स्टेडियम?

खिलाड़ी – सर अच्छा बना है, वहां पर मैं 10-12 दिन के लिए ट्रेनिंग करने गई थी, क्योंकि मैं मंदिर गई थी तो वहां पर ही ट्रेनिंग करके आई थी। और मैं वहां पे मतलब सेटल भी होना चाहती हूं क्योंकि मुझे काशी विश्वनाथ बहुत अच्छा लगता है सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – भोपाल में ट्रेनिंग कर रही थी ना?

खिलाड़ी – जी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – तो उज्जैन जाते थे कि नहीं?

खिलाड़ी – जी सर उज्जैन भी गई थी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – अच्छा महाकाल के पास भी गई।

खिलाड़ी – जी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – काशी विश्वनाथ के पास हो आई एक बार।

खिलाड़ी – जी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – सावन महीना तो अभी है।

खिलाड़ी – वहां घर जाके फिर उसके बाद जाऊंगी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – ठीक है।

खिलाड़ी – साई ने भी सर बहुत सपोर्ट किया है मुझे। इसके कारण ही मैं यहां तक पहुंची हूं सर। और मैं खेलो इंडिया स्कीम में भी थी 2018 में जो फर्स्ट खेलो इंडिया हुआ था, उसमें मेरा सिल्वर मेडल था, वहां पे भी मैंने आपको देखा था ओपनिंग सेरेमनी में, तो उसमें मेरा मेडल था, तो मेरे को स्कीम भी मिल गया और मैं यहां तक पहुंची हूं सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – स्पोर्ट्स व्यवस्था एक बात है, लेकिन देश मेडल तब प्राप्त करता है जब देश में स्पोर्ट्स कल्चर बनता है। दोस्तों आपने बहुत बड़ा काम किया है। देश का नाम रोशन किया है। आपको मैं बहुत बधाई देता हूं और आप विश्वास कीजिए आगे भी आप विजयी होंगे और फिर से एक बार यहीं पर हम मिलेंगे। बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं।

प्रधानमंत्री – ये लगातार तीसरी बार देश को मेडल दिलवाया है।

खिलाड़ी – थैंक यू सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत आशीर्वाद बेटा।

खिलाड़ी – और थैंक यू सो मच मैं सर के हाथ से लड्डू खा रही मेरा कल बर्थडे था तो आज सर के हाथ से…

प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत बधाई वाह।

प्रधानमंत्री – मुस्कुराओ यार ।

प्रधानमंत्री – जो खेलेगा वो खिलेगा।

 

****

MJPS/SS/ST/SS/DK/RK

2296978.title: Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav
2296978.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2296978.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav
On World Lion Day, Union Environment Minister reaffirms India’s commitment to Wildlife and Biodiversity Conservation
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi

On World Lion Day 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, celebrated India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation and reaffirmed the country’s unwavering commitment to protecting wildlife and biodiversity.

In a post on social media, the Minister noted that the Asiatic Lion population has steadily increased from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025. He attributed this achievement to the dedication of forest officials, conservationists, local communities and all those working tirelessly to protect the magnificent species.

 

🦁 On World Lion Day, we celebrate India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation.

India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to our unwavering commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. From protecting critical habitats to strengthening conservation… pic.twitter.com/7aJv98uRSG

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) August 10, 2026

 

Shri Yadav stated that India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to the country’s commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. He reaffirmed the resolve to safeguard India’s natural heritage and ensure that the roar of the Asiatic Lion continues to resonate for generations to come.

On the occasion, in a social media post, Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, stated that by protecting critical habitats, strengthening conservation programmes and fostering coexistence, India has shown the world that development and nature can thrive together.

 

On #WorldLionDay, we honour India’s extraordinary journey in conserving the majestic Asiatic Lion.

From 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025, this remarkable growth reflects the tireless efforts of forest officers, frontline workers, conservationists, local communities & countless… pic.twitter.com/FCkRYqPwEI

— Kirti Vardhan Singh (@KVSinghMPGonda) August 10, 2026

 

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced 'Project Lion' on 15th August, 2020, to ensure long term conservation of the big cat. Currently, the lion range has expanded from around 30,000 sq. km. in 2020 to nearly 35,000 sq. km.

The project adopts a landscape-level, holistic approach to biodiversity conservation, emphasising habitat enhancement, disease monitoring and veterinary support, scientific population tracking, technology-aided interventions, biodiversity protection, benefit sharing and community involvement.

  ***

VM/GS

2296968.title: PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance
2296968.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 11:47AM by PIB Delhi

PAIMANA – An Overview

Efficient monitoring of infrastructure projects is essential for timely implementation, transparency and governance. To support this, PAIMANA (Project Assessment, Infrastructure Monitoring and Analytics for Nation-Building) was launched on 25 September 2025 as a web-based platform for monitoring Central Sector infrastructure projects in India. The platform replaces the earlier OCMS-2006 (Online Computerized Monitoring System). Developed by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), PAIMANA is used for monitoring ongoing Central Sector infrastructure projects costing ₹150 crore or more.

MoSPI has launched a module called PAIMANA-CRIP on 08th July 2026, replacing DPIIT’s Integrated Project Monitoring Portal (IPMP), envisioned to evolve as Central Repository of Infrastructure Projects. The project-related data for PRAGATI (Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation), PMG and other review mechanisms would subsequently be sourced and updated through the same.

Over 20+ Ministries/Departments/ Implementing Agencies regularly update the information of projects on PAIMANA-CRIP through data entry or via API (Application Programming Interfaces) modes.

Currently, the Project Monitoring vertical of the PAIMANA portal is integrated with DPIIT’s IPMP/ IIG through API-based data exchange. Over 60 per cent of projects on PAIMANA are being updated automatically through APIs from the MIS or web platforms of respective Ministries/ Departments.

In addition to strengthening project monitoring, PAIMANA has expanded its role to support infrastructure performance monitoring through a dedicated Performance Monitoring Dashboard. Launched on 16th April, 2026, the dashboard tracks infrastructure performance across major sub-sectors through a comprehensive set of indicators. It marks a significant advancement towards data-driven governance and evidence-based policymaking.

 

Performance Monitoring Dashboard at a Glance

The Performance Monitoring Dashboard brings together performance indicators across key infrastructure sectors in a unified digital platform. The indicators are compiled from official data provided/published by the concerned Ministries and Departments and are updated periodically based on the latest available information. The dashboard presents these data through interactive visualizations and analytical tools, enabling users to monitor trends and assess sectoral performance over time.

Key Features of the Performance Monitoring Dashboard

  • The Performance Monitoring Dashboard is built on a comprehensive indicator framework developed in consultation with the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP). The framework aligns with the Harmonized Master List (HML) of Infrastructure (2022), issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), which serves as the national classification framework for infrastructure sectors eligible for policy support, investment planning and financing-related benefits.
  • Indicators have been streamlined to prevent overlap with established indices. Examples include the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and the Eight Core Industries.
  • A detailed indicator framework spans six infrastructure sub-sectors. These are Power, Civil Aviation, Telecommunications, Railways, Roads, and Ports, Shipping & Waterways.
  • The Performance Monitoring Dashboard has now been expanded to 165 indicators. This expansion includes the addition of 54 new indicators, significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of infrastructure performance monitoring.
  • A single digital interface allows monitoring of performance sector by sector. It offers interactive visualisation and time-series analysis for policymakers, researchers and stakeholders.
  • A centralised dashboard delivers one cross-sector view of infrastructure sectors. This capability deepens inter-sectoral analysis.
  • The current framework gauges sectoral performance through growth rates. It reviews year-on-year, month-on-month and cumulative growth, targets and capacity utilisation in chosen sectors.

The Revamped Monitoring Approach

The revamped approach marks a shift from measuring sectoral outputs (production) to assessing multi-dimensional infrastructure performance across the dimensions of access: which measure how widely infrastructure is available; quality: which assess its usefulness and reliability; fiscal cost & revenue: which assess allocation and use of financial resources for infrastructure; utilization: evaluate how efficiently infrastructure is used for its defined purpose; affordability: determine whether it is economically accessible to people. The above categorisation of indicators improves analysis by moving beyond simple output tracking to a more holistic evaluation of infrastructure performance across multiple dimensions, enabling informed policy decisions and targeted interventions.

 

Engaging Stakeholders

Stakeholders, including concerned Ministries and Departments, receive regular updates on their project execution. These updates draw on the data analytics generated within PAIMANA. Such analytics help them act wherever project execution needs attention.

  • Ongoing coordination takes place through monthly review meetings and other exchanges. This practice reinforces evidence-based monitoring by providing timely updates on performance indicators.
  • Login credentials for tailored dashboards are available with every Line Ministry and Department. Consequently, they can directly access the portal to review project progress.

 

Infrastructure Projects Monitored (Data as of June 2026)

  • As of June 2026, 1,847 ongoing projects were under watch across 17 Central Ministries and Departments. Together they carry a revised cost of ₹ 40.54 lakh crore.
  • Spending on these projects has so far reached ₹ 21.97 lakh crore. This equals about 54.18 per cent of the revised cost, reflecting steady advancement.
  • Many projects have reached advanced stages of completion. Around 709 projects (~39%) exceed 80% physical progress. About 337 projects (~19%) have passed 80% financial completion.
  • The Transport & Logistics sector leads in the number of ongoing projects. It holds 1,341 projects worth ₹22.32 lakh crore, reflecting the focus on connectivity.
  • The ongoing infrastructure projects include 769 mega projects, each costing ₹1,000 crore or more, worth ₹30.51 lakh crore.
  • They also include 1,078 major projects, each costing ₹150–1,000 crore, worth ₹5.10 lakh crore.

 

Ministry / Department-wise Progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways records the largest project count. It manages 1,022 projects (55%) with a revised cost share of Rs. 9.89 lakh crore (24%).
  • The Ministry of Railways is carrying out 255 projects (14%). These carry a combined revised cost of Rs. 8.69 lakh crore (21%).
  • The Ministry of Coal is running 121 projects (7%). Their combined revised cost stands at Rs. 2.22 lakh crore (6%).
  • Four other ministries/departments are also implementing a significant number of projects.

o The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas is managing 105 projects with a revised cost of ₹4.33 lakh crore.

o The Ministry of Power is handling 98 projects with a revised cost of ₹5.71 lakh crore.

o The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs is implementing 50 projects with a revised cost of ₹3.65 lakh crore.

o The Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation is managing 40 projects with a revised cost of ₹2.04 lakh crore.

  • The other 156 projects (8%) carry a combined revised cost of Rs. 4.02 lakh crore (10%). They span across several Ministries and Departments, such as Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports.

 

Towards Data-Driven Governance

The PAIMANA portal encapsulating modules of the Central repository of infrastructure projects along with outcomes as Reports/ dashboard on overview of Central sector projects costing ₹150 crores & above and the Performance monitoring dashboard would play significant stride towards transparency, efficiency and accountability. Their regular updates keep strengthening infrastructure oversight. They aid evidence-based policymaking and enable well-informed decisions. Overall, the effort promotes sustainable and inclusive infrastructure growth nationwide.

2296929.title: CHIEF OF THE NAVAL STAFF ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO MAURITIUS TO STRENGTHEN BILATERAL MARITIME COOPERATION
2296929.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
CHIEF OF THE NAVAL STAFF ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO MAURITIUS TO STRENGTHEN BILATERAL MARITIME COOPERATION
Posted On: 10 AUG 2026 9:28AM by PIB Delhi

Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), is on a four-day official visit to Mauritius from 10 to 13 Aug 2026. The visit is part of India's continued engagement to strengthen bilateral maritime cooperation and deepen defence ties with Mauritius, an extremely valued partner in the Indian Ocean Region.

During the visit, the CNS will interact with senior leadership of the Government of Mauritius and hold discussions on matters of mutual interest such as maritime security, defence cooperation, capacity building and military collaboration.

Such engagements are aimed at strengthening Indo-Mauritius cooperation in the maritime domain, enhancing operational-level linkages and consolidating the robust strategic partnership between India and Mauritius.

India and Mauritius share a close and enduring maritime partnership. The Indian Navy engages regularly with the National Coast Guard through training exchanges, operational interactions including Joint Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Surveillance, port visits and hydrographic surveys. Both countries also participate and engage with each other in multilateral forums and cooperative initiatives. Mauritius has been a regular participant in key Indian Navy initiatives such as the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, MILAN, International Fleet Review, Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR and Exercise AIKEYME, aptly reflecting the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) they share.

The visit of Admiral Krishna Swaminathan to Mauritius after assuming charge as the Chief of the Naval Staff underscores the priority India accords to the friendship it shares with Mauritius, anchored in mutual respect, trust and a shared commitment to maritime security, regional cooperation and stability in the Indian Ocean Region.

2296879.title: ICoAS fraternity reaffirms commitment to cost optimisation for Atmanirbhar Bharat on ICoAS day 2026
2296879.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
ICoAS fraternity reaffirms commitment to cost optimisation for Atmanirbhar Bharat on ICoAS day 2026
Secretary Expenditure Shri V. Vualnam expressed his commendation for valuable tireless efforts of ICoAS officers in cost management of Government of India
Defence Secretary Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh: Financial prudence and commercial expertise assume critical importance during unprecedented transformation of defence sector currently
Secretary Defence Production Shri. Sanjeev Kumar: ICoAS officers support in cost management goes beyond reducing expenditure, and enables better investment decisions
Posted On: 09 AUG 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi

Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Defence, Ministry of Defence, graced the Foundation Day celebration of the Indian Cost Accounts Service (ICoAS), organised under the aegis of the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, as the Chief Guest, in New Delhi today. Shri. Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary, Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, was present on the occasion as the Guest of Honour. This year's celebration was observed under the theme "Role of ICoAS Officers in Cost Optimization for Atmanirbhar Bharat", reflecting the growing significance of cost and fiscal efficiency in furthering India's pursuit of self-reliance leading to Viksit Bharat.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Defence lauded the professionalism, analytical acumen and steadfast dedication of ICoAS officers in strengthening cost management practices across Government Ministries and Departments. He observed that the Service has consistently played a catalytic role in advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat through judicious cost optimization, prudent resource utilisation and robust financial oversight, particularly in Defence Sector.

In his address as Guest of Honour, Shri. Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary, Department of Defence Production, drew attention to the increasing relevance of cost accounting expertise in bolstering indigenous manufacturing capabilities thereby not only reducing India's reliance on imports, but also be competitive in export market. He commended the unique and strategic role of ICoAS officers with the Defence Production ecosystem and called for reinvention of the service and its functioning in the changing defence acquisition scenarios and to develop deeper synergy between ICoAS officers and strategic sectors in furtherance of national self-reliance.

Shri V. Vualnam, Secretary, Department of Expenditure (DoE), Ministry of Finance, conveyed his warm greetings to the officers on the occasion of ICoAS Day 2026 through a video message. He highlighted the valuable contribution of ICoAS officers towards effective cost management in the Government of India. He further emphasized that, with the increasing participation of the private sector and the growing adoption of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat, ICoAS officers will have a significant role in ensuring cost efficiency, appropriate risk allocation and sound project structuring.

On the occasion, a commemorative e-brochure of the ICoAS was released, chronicling the evolution, key functions, notable achievements and capacity-building initiatives undertaken by the Service.

Earlier in the programme, Shri Anand Kumar Pal, Chief Adviser (Cost) and Head of ICoAS conveyed his warm wishes to the officers of ICoAS service and urged them to embrace technology and innovation to be the financial analysts for the Government of India. He also stressed the officers to uphold the highest standards of integrity and professionalism and to adopt latest financial modelling tools; advanced techniques for data visualisation; analytical frameworks that support farsighted financial advice and sound policy design for moving towards Viksit Bharat.

Shri. Rohin Koppuravuri, Joint Director (Cost) gave a presentation on the Service's journey, evolution, its contribution and the future course of action to be undertaken to meet the evolving demands of public financial management and to ensure “Maximum Value for every Rupee spent”.

In recognition of outstanding contribution, six young ICoAS officers were felicitated by Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Defence, with 'Sarvottam', 'Ati Uttam’,'Uttam' and 'Protsahan' appreciation certificates instituted to encourage and acknowledge the meritorious efforts of young officers of the Service.

The inaugural session was followed by two engaging technical sessions marking the ICoAS commitment to innovation, continuous learning and professional excellence.

In the first technical session, Shri Nandkumaram spoke on the "Use of Artificial Intelligence in Public Financial Management", elaborating on the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence in enhancing efficiency and AI Interventions across Public Finance Value Chain for cost and financial management functions across Government.

The second technical session saw Shri Arvind Raj address the officers on "Stress Management", sharing valuable insights and practical strategies to help officers maintain mental well-being and professional resilience amidst demanding official responsibilities.

The celebration drew enthusiastic participation from senior officials across Ministries and Departments, reaffirming the indispensable role of ICoAS in policy formulation, cost management and efficient public expenditure.

ICoAS Day 2026 thus served as a valuable platform for capacity building, knowledge exchange and strategic dialogue, reinforcing the Service's unwavering commitment to a self-reliant and economically resilient Viksit Bharat.

2296861.title: Runway Excursion Incident Involving Cessna C172 trainer Aircraft at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra
2296861.body_html:
Ministry of Civil Aviation
Runway Excursion Incident Involving Cessna C172 trainer Aircraft at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra
Posted On: 09 AUG 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

A runway excursion incident involving a Cessna C172 type aircraft, registration VT-SEX, operated by Academy of Carver Aviation, a DGCA approved Flying Training Organization occurred at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra, on 09 August 2026 at approximately 12:25 PM.

The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies (CL Emergencies) training exercise. The aircraft was under the command of Capt. Chirag Shashikant Doifode, Flight Instructor with trainee Abhijeet Jundre on board.

The aircraft taxied out at approximately 0639 UTC (1209 IST) for the scheduled training exercise. During the exercise, the aircraft entered the runway through Link Bravo and lined up at the threshold of Runway 29, where a rejected take-off exercise practice was carried out. Subsequently, the aircraft lined up at the threshold of Runway 11 and another rejected take-off exercise was carried out.

During the course of the exercise, the aircraft was unable to stop within the paved runway surface and subsequently veered off the extended paved surface beyond the threshold of Runway 29 towards the right side, resulting in a runway excursion.

There were no injuries or fatalities reported. The aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear. A detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities.

The DGCA Air Safety team is proceeding to the site to conduct a preliminary investigation and ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident. Further information will be shared as and when it is verified and becomes available.

2296858.title: ‘The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon’ — MoS Raksha Khadse
2296858.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2296858.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
‘The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon’ — MoS Raksha Khadse
Appeal to turn the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva – Viksit Bharat’ campaign into a people’s movement; Emphasis on collective action by spiritual institutions, saints, administration and youth
Posted On: 09 AUG 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

A special meeting of representatives from spiritual institutions, saints and seers, public representatives, administration, voluntary organizations and social bodies was held today at the District Planning Bhavan, Collector Office, Jalgaon, to give a widespread people’s movement character to the nationwide ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva – Viksit Bharat’ campaign launched on the appeal of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports, Smt. Raksha Khadse, addressed and guided the meeting through video conferencing.  

Also present were Minister Shri Sanjay Savkare, MLA Shri Raju Bhole, District Collector Shri Rohan Ghuge, Superintendent of Police Shri Shrikant Dhivare, CEO Zilla Parishad Smt. Karishma Nair, District Youth Officer, MY Bharat Shri Abhishek Chavare, along with other administrative officials.  

Mahamandaleshwar Swami Janardan Hari Ji Maharaj graced the meeting with his presence. Representatives of various spiritual and religious institutions, saints, voluntary organizations and social sector also participated.

“The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon”

Guiding the meeting, Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse urged for mass public participation in the Nasha Mukti campaign in Jalgaon district.

She said, The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon. The energy of our youth should be used not in addiction, but in nation-building. Our effort will be to take the resolve that started from Jalgaon to every family and every young person and transform it into a widespread mass movement. A healthy, empowered and addiction-free youth generation is the real strength of a Viksit Bharat. For building a Nasha Mukt society, it is essential that along with the government, saints, spiritual institutions, social organizations, educational institutions and youth come forward together.”

Decisive role of spiritual institutions and saints

The meeting highlighted that given the wide reach of spiritual institutions and saints across all sections of society in Jalgaon district, their role in taking the message of Nasha Mukti to every village is extremely important. It was emphasized that they should continuously run awareness programs to convey the importance of an addiction-free lifestyle, self-discipline, positive thinking and healthy living to the youth.

Mahamandaleshwar Swami Janardan Hari Ji Maharaj said that the role of family, society and spiritual institutions is crucial in character building of youth.  

“To keep youth away from addiction, it is necessary to build their confidence, values and positive outlook towards life. Spiritual institutions and saints will actively participate in this awareness work,” he stated.

Focus on channelizing youth energy in positive directions

It was stated that mere awareness is not enough in de-addiction efforts. Youth must be connected with positive opportunities in sports, education, skill development, employment, volunteering and nation-building. The need for MY Bharat, NSS, youth clubs, educational institutions and social organizations to work in coordination to channelize youth energy into constructive and positive work was expressed.

Active participation of public representatives

Speaking on the occasion, Minister Shri Sanjay Savkare stressed the need for all sections of society to actively participate with the government in the Nasha Mukti campaign.

“Youth are the future of the country. Along with awareness, it is necessary to connect them with positive and constructive initiatives to keep them away from addiction. If this campaign gets public participation, its impact will certainly be widespread,” he said.

MLA Shri Raju Bhole emphasized the need to run continuous local initiatives to take the message of Nasha Mukti to the youth of Jalgaon city as well as the district.  

“For a Nasha Mukt society, every family and every citizen must participate in this effort. Giving youth the right direction and positive opportunities is our collective responsibility,” he said.

Action through coordination of administration and social organizations

The meeting discussed implementing continuous activities through coordination of MY Bharat, NSS, youth clubs, educational institutions, voluntary organizations, sports bodies, spiritual institutions and local administration for effective execution of the campaign.  

An appeal was made for various organizations to actively participate through their platforms to take the message of Nasha Mukti to every village in Jalgaon district, create awareness among youth and build a positive environment to stay away from addiction. 

Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, it was resolved to give the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva – Viksit Bharat’ campaign the form of a widespread people’s movement in Jalgaon district and take the message of Nasha Mukti to every village, every family and every youth.

2296842.title: INDIAN NAVY–US NAVY EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE DISPOSAL EXERCISE 2026 TO COMMENCE AT SOUTHERN NAVAL COMMAND, KOCHI
2296842.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY–US NAVY EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE DISPOSAL EXERCISE 2026 TO COMMENCE AT SOUTHERN NAVAL COMMAND, KOCHI
Posted On: 09 AUG 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy–US Navy Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Exercise 2026 is scheduled to be conducted at Southern Naval Command, Kochi, from 10 to 14 Aug 2026. The bilateral exercise aims to enhance interoperability and strengthen professional cooperation between the specialist diving and EOD teams of the two navies.

The five-day exercise will comprise Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-training, equipment demonstrations and scenario-based practical exercises. The programme will facilitate the exchange of contemporary EOD methodologies, emerging technologies and Best Practices, while providing both sides an opportunity to gain insights into each other’s capabilities, operational concepts and employment philosophies.

The exercise is designed to promote collaborative learning and operational synergy, enabling personnel from both navies to refine procedures, enhance mutual understanding and strengthen their ability to respond effectively to complex and evolving EOD challenges.

The Indian Navy and US Navy have been conducting joint Salvage and EOD exercises since 2005. The forthcoming engagement marks the eighth edition of this specialised bilateral training exercise and underscores the enduring commitment of the two navies towards enhancing interoperability, sharing operational expertise and strengthening cooperation in specialised maritime operations.
